## Performance and Reliability Comparison

Performance is one of the most important factors when choosing a proxy provider. A slow or unreliable proxy network can ruin your data pipelines and cost you time and money.

Oxylabs publishes detailed performance data. Its residential proxies average a 0.41-second response time, while datacenter proxies clock in at just 0.25 seconds. An independent study by Proxyway in 2024 confirmed Oxylabs’ average success rate of 99.82%. The ISP and Dedicated ISP products achieve a 99.9% success rate on most major targets.

Shifter advertises 99.99% uptime for its network. However, uptime and success rate are different metrics. Shifter does not publish independently verified success-rate data, which makes direct performance comparisons difficult.

Oxylabs uses the QUIC protocol for its residential proxy network, reducing latency and improving connection reliability. Its infrastructure is backed by ISO 27001-certified data centers and covered by Technology Errors and Omissions insurance and Cyber Insurance through Lloyd’s of London. Shifter mentions certified data centers but does not provide the same level of transparency in certification details.

For high-volume, mission-critical scraping operations, Oxylabs has a clear performance edge, according to publicly available data. Shifter may perform well for smaller workloads, but it lacks the third-party validation to confirm enterprise-level reliability.

## Use Cases: Who Should Use Each Provider?

### **Oxylabs is Best For**

Oxylabs shines for enterprise-level web intelligence tasks. If your business depends on large-scale data extraction, AI training data, market research, ad verification, or competitive pricing intelligence, Oxylabs has the infrastructure to support it. Its mobile proxies make it ideal for app testing and geo-targeted mobile scraping. Its AI Studio and integrations with tools like LangChain and CrewAI make it a strong choice for AI and LLM development teams.

Media companies, cybersecurity firms, travel aggregators, and financial data providers will find Oxylabs’ product suite comprehensive and well-suited to their needs. The dedicated account management, enterprise pricing tiers, and ISP proxy selection also make it attractive for larger procurement teams.

### **Shifter is Best For**

Shifter is a good fit for smaller teams and individual developers who want simple, affordable proxy access without a steep learning curve. Its rotating residential proxies work well for basic scraping, market research, and ad verification at modest volumes. The sneaker proxy offering is a niche but clear use case where Shifter explicitly positions itself.

If you are running low- to mid-volume scraping tasks and do not need mobile proxies, ISP proxies, or AI-powered scraping tools, Shifter offers a cost-effective entry point. Its cloud hosting add-on is also useful for teams that want to run scraping infrastructure close to proxy endpoints.

## Final Verdict

Both Oxylabs and Shifter are legitimate proxy providers with real-world use cases, but they serve very different audiences.

Oxylabs is the stronger choice for businesses that need scale, reliability, compliance, and a comprehensive product ecosystem. If you are running enterprise-level scraping, building AI training datasets, doing ad verification across multiple geographies, or need a partner with proven uptime and independently verified performance, Oxylabs is the clear winner. Its investment in AI tools, developer integrations, and customer success resources puts it in a different league.

Shifter is a solid option for individuals, small teams, and developers who need affordable proxy access for lower-volume tasks. Its simple interface, port-based pricing, and sneaker proxy offering make it appealing for a specific slice of the market. It is a capable provider within its niche, even if it cannot match Oxylabs on depth or scale.

In short, choose Oxylabs if you need enterprise-grade infrastructure and comprehensive features. Choose Shifter if you are starting small and want simplicity at a lower upfront cost.

Performance is one of the most important factors when choosing a proxy provider. A slow or unreliable proxy network can waste time and money. Here is how Oxylabs and SOAX compare on the metrics that matter most.

Oxylabs reports an average residential proxy response time of 0.41 seconds. ## Company Background and Evolution

### NetNut

[NetNut](/providers/netnut/) was founded in Israel in 2017 and has since grown into one of the largest proxy providers globally. Over the years, NetNut has built a reputation for reliable infrastructure and enterprise-grade service. NetNut serves a broad customer base that spans Fortune 500 companies, established scraping agencies, and data resellers. Its scale, network diversity, and dedicated account management make it particularly attractive to organizations with high-volume, recurring data-collection needs. ### Nimble

[Nimble](/providers/nimble/), founded in 2022 and registered in the United States, is a fast-growing company with a strong team in Israel. Despite being new to the market, Nimble has raised several rounds of venture capital and quickly expanded to around 80 employees, with more hiring ongoing. Their goal is not just to provide proxies but to change how businesses access and use live web data.

Unlike traditional proxy vendors, Nimble sees itself as a data layer company. Their platform offers residential proxies, a Website Unblocker, SERP Scraper API, e-commerce APIs, and custom Web Search Agents that help businesses extract and stream data into systems like Databricks and Amazon S3. While newer and with a smaller IP pool than competitors like [Bright Data](/providers/bright-data/) and NetNut, Nimble is growing fast and attracting enterprise clients.

The key differentiator here is sourcing: IPRoyal’s [residential proxies](/residential-proxies/) come entirely from its proprietary Pawns.app, ensuring ethical sourcing through transparent user agreements. This gives IPRoyal a moral advantage, though the smaller pool size may limit large-scale operations.

The catch with IPRoyal is that without KYC verification, you only get access to 40% of the pool, and various high-value targets (LinkedIn, banks, government websites) remain blocked. This restriction doesn’t apply to Decodo’s service in the same way.

### **Datacenter Proxies**

**Decodo** offers [datacenter proxies](/datacenter-proxies/) from around 15 countries in [shared](/shared-proxies/), [dedicated](/dedicated-proxies/), and pool-based formats. These are designed for speed-critical applications and come with the reliability expected from a mature provider.

**IPRoyal** provides datacenter proxies across 60+ locations, giving it a wider geographic footprint. The proxies come in dedicated lists, and the provider has historically targeted specific niches like sneakerheads with specialized endpoints for stores like Nike.

### **ISP Proxies**

Both providers offer [ISP proxies](/isp-proxies/) (static residential), which combine the speed of datacenter proxies with the legitimacy of residential IPs.

**Decodo** positions these as very similar to datacenter proxies, offering them across multiple countries with reliable performance.

**IPRoyal** provides ISP proxies in over 30 countries, also in dedicated list formats. Pricing starts competitively at $2.00 per proxy.

### **Mobile Proxies**

**Decodo** offers mobile proxies from real smartphones connected to 3G/4G/5G carrier networks worldwide, starting at $2.25/GB. These are genuine mobile IPs that provide authentic mobile traffic footprints.

**IPRoyal** provides mobile proxies based on dedicated dongles in over 15 countries, starting at $10.11/day (approximately 4.5 million IPs). The dongle-based approach offers stability for long-session use cases.

## FAQ

**What are Reddit dataset providers?** Reddit dataset providers collect, aggregate, and deliver structured data from Reddit including posts, comments, upvotes, subreddit activity, user sentiment, and discussion threads. These providers offer datasets to support AI training, sentiment analysis, market research, and competitive intelligence activities.  **How much do Reddit datasets typically cost?** Reddit dataset pricing varies by provider and data volume. Premium services like Bright Data start at $250/month for marketplace datasets. Free options exist through Kaggle and Academic Torrents for academic research. Most providers offer pay-per-record pricing and subscription-based plans with tiered access.  **What types of Reddit data can I collect?** Available Reddit data includes posts (text, media, timestamps), comments and replies, upvotes/downvotes, subreddit metadata, user activity patterns, awards, flair data, sentiment scores, and discussion threads. Data is typically delivered in CSV, JSON, XLSX, or Parquet formats for easy integration.  **Which Reddit dataset provider offers the best data quality?** Bright Data leads with customizable Reddit datasets, multiple delivery formats (JSON, CSV, Parquet), and GDPR/CCPA compliance. Kaggle excels for community-driven datasets with pre-built notebooks for machine learning. Oxylabs offers enterprise-grade scraping solutions with high scalability and real-time data access.  **Is scraping Reddit data legal?** Using Reddit’s official API and authorized dataset providers is the compliant way to access Reddit data. Reddit updated its API terms in 2023-2024 restricting unauthorized scraping. Reputable providers like Bright Data and Oxylabs ensure data collection complies with Reddit’s policies and GDPR/CCPA regulations.  **Can I get free Reddit datasets?** Yes, Kaggle and Academic Torrents offer free Reddit datasets covering sentiment analysis, subreddit activity, and comment threads. These are ideal for academic research and prototyping, though they may lack real-time updates and customization options available with premium providers.  **What is the difference between Reddit API and dataset providers?** Reddit’s official API has rate limits and access restrictions introduced in 2023 with significant pricing changes. Dataset providers offer pre-collected, structured data with unlimited access, historical archives, multiple delivery formats, and no technical complexity. Providers are better suited for enterprise projects and comprehensive analysis.

## FAQ

**What are YouTube dataset providers?** YouTube dataset providers are companies that collect, aggregate, and deliver structured data from YouTube including video metadata, engagement metrics, comments, channel statistics, subscriber data, and trending information. These providers offer datasets to support content analysis, sentiment research, trend monitoring, and machine learning projects.  **How much do YouTube datasets typically cost?** YouTube dataset pricing varies by provider and data volume. Premium services like Bright Data start at $250/month, while Oxylabs offers enterprise-grade solutions with custom pricing. Free options exist through platforms like Kaggle for academic research. Most providers offer pay-per-usage models and tiered subscription plans.  **What types of YouTube data can I access?** Available YouTube data includes video titles, descriptions, tags, view counts, likes, dislikes, comments, subscriber counts, channel metadata, engagement rates, geographic data, trending topics, and historical performance metrics. Data is typically delivered in formats like CSV, JSON, XLSX, and Parquet.  **Which YouTube dataset provider offers the best data quality?** Bright Data leads in YouTube data quality with comprehensive video and channel datasets, real-time scraping capabilities, and multiple delivery formats (CSV, JSON, Parquet). Oxylabs excels for large-scale, high-speed extraction with multilingual support. Apify provides customizable scraping solutions with affordable pay-per-result pricing.  **Is it legal to scrape YouTube data?** Scraping publicly available YouTube data is generally permissible when done through official APIs and authorized dataset providers. Reputable providers like Bright Data use compliant methodologies, respect rate limits, and follow platform guidelines. Users should ensure compliance with YouTube terms of service and data privacy regulations like GDPR and CCPA.  **Can I get free YouTube datasets?** Yes, platforms like Kaggle offer free YouTube datasets for research and machine learning projects. These include video metadata, trending data, and comment datasets. However, free datasets may not be real-time or as comprehensive as those from premium providers like Bright Data or Oxylabs.  **What is the difference between YouTube Data API and dataset providers?** YouTube’s official Data API has strict quotas, rate limits, and access restrictions. Dataset providers offer pre-collected, structured data with unlimited access, historical archives, multiple delivery formats, and no technical complexity. Providers bypass API limitations while ensuring compliance and data quality for enterprise-scale projects.

## FAQ

**What are Facebook dataset providers?** Facebook dataset providers collect, aggregate, and deliver structured data from Facebook including user profiles, page analytics, engagement metrics, and sentiment data. These providers offer datasets to support brand monitoring, market research, competitive analysis, and audience insights without requiring direct API access.  **How much do Facebook datasets typically cost?** Facebook dataset pricing starts from $250/month for marketplace datasets. Custom data extraction services range from $500-1,000+ monthly depending on volume and complexity. Enterprise solutions like Brandwatch offer custom pricing for comprehensive social listening. Free options exist through platforms like Kaggle for academic research.  **What types of Facebook data are available?** Available Facebook data includes user profiles (demographics, job titles, locations), page analytics (followers, engagement rates), post content (text, images, videos), comments and reactions, ad performance data, audience insights, and sentiment analysis. Coverage varies by provider and compliance requirements.  **Which Facebook dataset provider offers the best data quality?** Bright Data leads with high-quality, validated Facebook data in multiple formats (JSON, CSV, Parquet) with GDPR/CCPA compliance. Brandwatch excels for AI-powered sentiment analysis and real-time monitoring. People Data Labs specializes in profile-level professional data for B2B applications.  **Are Facebook datasets GDPR compliant?** Reputable providers like Bright Data, Zyte, and People Data Labs ensure GDPR and CCPA compliance through ethical data collection, proper consent mechanisms, and privacy controls. They focus on publicly available data and implement data anonymization where required. Always verify provider compliance certifications.  **Can I use Facebook data for marketing?** Yes, Facebook datasets support various marketing applications including audience research, competitive analysis, sentiment monitoring, influencer identification, and campaign optimization. Ensure compliance with data privacy regulations and use data ethically for legitimate business purposes like market research and brand monitoring.  **What is the difference between Facebook Graph API and dataset providers?** Facebook’s Graph API has strict access restrictions and limited data availability since privacy changes. Dataset providers offer broader data access, historical archives, pre-processed information, and simplified integration. Providers aggregate publicly available data while ensuring compliance with privacy regulations.

## FAQ

**What are Twitter dataset providers?** Twitter dataset providers are companies that collect, aggregate, and deliver structured data from Twitter/X including tweets, user profiles, engagement metrics, hashtags, trends, and sentiment data. These providers offer datasets to support social listening, sentiment analysis, trend monitoring, and market research activities.  **How much do Twitter datasets typically cost?** Twitter dataset pricing varies by provider and data volume. Entry-level options start at $2.50 per 1,000 records for historical data, while real-time scraping starts at $1.50 per 1,000 records. Enterprise solutions with advanced analytics can cost $500-800+ monthly. Most providers offer free trials and pay-as-you-go models.  **What types of Twitter data can I access?** Available Twitter data includes tweets (text, media, timestamps), user profiles (bios, followers, following), engagement metrics (likes, retweets, replies), hashtag performance, trending topics, sentiment scores, geolocation data, and historical archives spanning multiple years for trend analysis.  **Which Twitter dataset provider offers the best data quality?** Bright Data leads in Twitter data quality with 22M+ verified records, real-time scraping capabilities, and multiple delivery formats (CSV, JSON, Parquet). They offer 99.99% uptime and 24/7 support. Tweet Binder excels for hashtag analytics, while Apify provides customizable scraping solutions.  **Is it legal to scrape Twitter data?** Scraping publicly available Twitter data is generally legal when done responsibly. Reputable providers like Bright Data use compliant methodologies, respect rate limits, and follow platform guidelines. However, users should ensure compliance with Twitter’s terms of service and data privacy regulations like GDPR and CCPA.  **Can I get historical Twitter data?** Yes, providers like Bright Data maintain extensive historical Twitter archives with 22M+ records. Awesome Twitter Data offers free open-source historical datasets for academic research. Historical data is valuable for trend analysis, sentiment tracking over time, and training machine learning models.  **What is the difference between Twitter API and dataset providers?** Twitter’s official API has strict rate limits, access restrictions, and high costs. Dataset providers offer pre-collected, structured data with unlimited access, historical archives, multiple delivery formats, and no technical complexity. Providers bypass API limitations while ensuring compliance and data quality.

## 7. Bridge Interactive

Bridge Interactive offers an official way to request Zillow Group data access through the Bridge API platform. It is built for developers and organizations that want approved, programmatic access to selected Zillow datasets. Current options include U.S. Public Records, Zillow Zestimates, and Zillow Group Economic Data. After approval, users can connect through a native API and pull the data into their own tools or apps. Bridge also provides documentation, sample API calls, and an API explorer to simplify integration. Strong rules apply to protect Zillow’s data. Data must be displayed dynamically, and local storage is not allowed. This option works best for compliant, link-backed applications.

### **Key Features: **

- **Public Records (US):** Property records, tax assessments, and transaction history across ~148M properties

- **Zestimates API:** Current home and rental Zestimates available on Zillow.com

- **Econ Data API:** Housing market metrics that also appear on Zillow’s data pages

- **Official access workflow:** Request access through an application and approval process

- **Developer tools:** Documentation, sample calls, and an API explorer for testing

- **Compliance rules:** Data must be displayed with links back to Zillow and cannot be stored locally

### **Pros**

- Official, approved access to Zillow Group datasets

- Useful for building compliant tools and apps

- Includes documentation and developer explorer tools

### **Cons**

- Local data storage is not allowed

- Must link back to Zillow

- Usage is limited and approval depends on your use case

### **Pricing**

- Not publicly listed (access depends on approval and terms)

- Usage limit: up to 1,000 calls/day per dataset after review and approval

The demand for real estate data is growing fast. Zillow datasets are among the most valuable sources of property information. ## FAQ

**What are Zillow dataset providers?** Zillow dataset providers collect and deliver structured property data from Zillow including listings, prices, Zestimates, property details, locations, and market trends. These providers support real estate analysis, investment research, market intelligence, and AI/ML model development for property valuation and prediction.  **How much do Zillow datasets typically cost?** Zillow dataset pricing varies by provider. Bright Data starts at $0.0025 per record with $250 minimum orders. Oxylabs offers plans from $49-249/month with pay-per-result options. Apify provides pay-as-you-go pricing with free monthly credits. Enterprise solutions offer custom pricing based on volume and requirements.  **What types of Zillow data are available?** Available Zillow data includes property listings (address, price, status), Zestimates (current and historical), property details (bedrooms, bathrooms, square footage), photos, descriptions, market trends, sale history, tax assessments, and neighborhood data. Coverage spans millions of U.S. properties.  **Which Zillow dataset provider offers the best data quality?** Bright Data leads with massive Zillow datasets, AI-based filtering, multiple delivery formats (JSON, CSV, Parquet), and enterprise-grade infrastructure. Oxylabs excels for real-time extraction with high scalability. Bridge Interactive offers official Zillow API access for compliant applications.  **Is it legal to scrape Zillow data?** Scraping publicly available Zillow data is generally permissible when done ethically. Reputable providers use compliant methodologies and respect platform guidelines. Bridge Interactive offers official API access for approved use cases. Always ensure GDPR/CCPA compliance when handling property data.  **Can I get historical Zillow data?** Yes, providers like Bright Data offer historical Zillow datasets with regular update schedules (monthly, quarterly, or custom). Historical data supports trend analysis, market forecasting, and property valuation models. Some providers maintain archives spanning multiple years of property listings and prices.  **What can I do with Zillow datasets?** Zillow datasets support real estate investment analysis, property valuation models, market trend research, competitive intelligence, lead generation, price prediction algorithms, and portfolio management. Data is used by investors, analysts, proptech companies, and AI developers for strategic decision-making.

## Conclusion

The real estate data market is filled with a wide variety of providers, each offering unique solutions for industry professionals. Bright Data, with its comprehensive datasets and global coverage, stands out as the leader. However, other providers like ATTOM, Datarade, and CoreLogic also offer valuable data solutions tailored to specific needs and regions. By evaluating your data requirements, coverage needs, and budget, you can select the provider that best suits your business goals.

## FAQ

**What are real estate data providers?** Real estate data providers collect, aggregate, and deliver structured property information including listings, ownership records, transaction history, valuations, market trends, and demographics. These providers support investors, agents, lenders, and researchers with data for analysis, valuation, and strategic decision-making.  **How much do real estate datasets typically cost?** Real estate data pricing varies widely. Bright Data starts at $250 for 100,000 records. PropertyShark starts at $94.95/month. Enterprise solutions like CoStar and CoreLogic offer custom subscription pricing ranging from hundreds to thousands monthly based on data access and features.  **What types of real estate data are available?** Available real estate data includes property listings, ownership records, transaction history, tax assessments, valuations (Zestimates, AVMs), market trends, demographics, zoning information, foreclosure data, rental market analytics, and commercial property details including tenant and lease information.  **Which real estate data provider offers the best coverage?** Bright Data offers global coverage with customizable datasets from multiple sources. ATTOM provides comprehensive U.S. data with 70B+ rows and 9,000+ attributes. CoStar leads for commercial real estate globally. CoreLogic excels for mortgage and financial risk data with 50+ years of historical records.  **What is the difference between residential and commercial real estate data?** Residential data focuses on single-family homes, condos, and apartments with valuations, sale prices, and neighborhood metrics. Commercial data covers office, retail, industrial, and multifamily properties with tenant information, lease terms, cap rates, and market analytics. Providers often specialize in one segment.  **Can I access real estate data through APIs?** Yes, most providers offer API access for real-time data integration. Bright Data, ATTOM, Zillow, and Cherre provide RESTful APIs and GraphQL endpoints. APIs enable automated data retrieval, custom queries, and integration with analytics platforms, CRMs, and business intelligence tools.  **How current is real estate data from providers?** Data freshness varies by provider and pricing tier. Premium providers like Bright Data and ATTOM offer daily or real-time updates. Standard subscriptions typically provide weekly or monthly refreshes. Historical data archives span decades for trend analysis and market forecasting applications.

## FAQ

**What are eCommerce dataset providers?** eCommerce dataset providers collect and deliver structured data from online retailers and marketplaces. They provide product information pricing inventory availability customer reviews seller details and marketplace metrics from platforms like Amazon Walmart Shopify and other eCommerce sites to support competitive analysis pricing strategies and market research.  **How accurate is eCommerce dataset information?** Leading providers like Bright Data and Oxylabs maintain 95%+ accuracy through automated validation, real-time scraping, and quality control processes. Data accuracy depends on update frequency, source reliability, and provider methodology. Premium providers offer daily or real-time updates, while budget options may update weekly or monthly.  **What can I do with eCommerce datasets?** eCommerce datasets support dynamic pricing strategies, competitive product analysis, market trend identification, inventory optimization, review sentiment analysis, seller performance tracking, and product catalog enrichment. Retailers use this data for pricing decisions, marketplace sellers optimize listings, and analysts track market share and category trends.  **Which platforms do eCommerce dataset providers cover?** Top providers cover major platforms including Amazon, Walmart, eBay, Etsy, Target, Best Buy, Home Depot, Wayfair, IKEA, Sephora, AliExpress, and regional marketplaces. Bright Data offers the widest coverage with 1000+ supported eCommerce sites, while specialized providers may focus on specific platforms or regions.  **How often are eCommerce datasets updated?** Update frequencies range from real-time (continuous monitoring) to daily, weekly, or monthly, depending on provider and pricing tier. Dynamic pricing applications require daily or real-time updates, while market research projects may only need weekly or monthly refreshes. Premium tiers from providers like Bright Data and Oxylabs offer customizable update schedules.  **Is web scraping eCommerce sites legal?** Web scraping publicly available eCommerce data is generally legal when done responsibly, but providers must comply with website terms of service, robots.txt files, and data privacy regulations. Reputable providers like Bright Data use compliant methodologies, respect rate limits, and ensure ethical data collection practices that align with legal frameworks.  **What data fields are included in eCommerce datasets?** Standard fields include product names, descriptions, prices, images, SKUs, brands, categories, availability status, seller information, customer ratings, review counts, shipping details, and product specifications. Advanced datasets may include historical pricing, inventory trends, competitor comparisons, and review sentiment scores.

## FAQ

**What are LinkedIn dataset providers?** LinkedIn dataset providers collect and deliver structured professional data from LinkedIn including user profiles company details job listings skills endorsements connections and career histories. These providers offer verified datasets to support B2B lead generation recruitment talent mapping competitive intelligence and market research without requiring manual LinkedIn scraping or API access.  **How do LinkedIn dataset providers collect data legally?** Reputable providers like Bright Data and Coresignal use ethical scraping of publicly available LinkedIn data, comply with data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA), employ proxy networks to avoid detection, and focus on professional information rather than personal data. They respect platform terms while providing compliant access to business-critical information.  **What types of LinkedIn data are available in datasets?** Available data includes professional profiles (names, titles, companies, locations, experience, education, skills), company information (size, industry, headquarters, employee counts), job listings (titles, descriptions, requirements, locations), connections, endorsements, and engagement metrics. Advanced datasets offer enriched data with email addresses and phone numbers.  **How accurate are LinkedIn datasets?** Premium providers like Bright Data maintain 90-95% accuracy through continuous validation, real-time updates, and data quality processes. Accuracy depends on update frequency, source methodology, and enrichment techniques. Providers offering recent data (updated daily or weekly) deliver higher accuracy than those with monthly or quarterly refreshes.  **What is the difference between LinkedIn scraping and dataset providers?** LinkedIn scraping involves manually extracting data using automated tools, requiring technical expertise, proxy management, and anti-detection measures. Dataset providers offer ready-to-use, structured, validated data with regular updates, compliance guarantees, and support, eliminating technical complexity and legal risks associated with DIY scraping.  **Can I use LinkedIn data for cold outreach?** Yes, but compliance is crucial. Use data from GDPR-compliant providers, ensure legitimate business interest, provide opt-out mechanisms, and follow CAN-SPAM and GDPR requirements. LinkedIn data supports targeted B2B outreach when used ethically, but mass unsolicited contact or spam violates platform terms and regulations.  **How much do LinkedIn datasets cost?** Pricing starts at $0.0025 per record (minimum $250 orders) for basic profile data. Comprehensive datasets with enriched information cost more, typically $500-2,000 for 100,000-200,000 records. Enterprise solutions with real-time updates and custom filtering can reach thousands monthly. Pricing varies by data depth, update frequency, and volume.

Choosing the right business dataset provider depends on your specific needs. Whether you require massive datasets, real-time data verification, or specialized coverage in Europe or North America, there’s a provider suited for every type of business. Bright Data, with its large-scale, customizable datasets, leads the pack, but other providers like ZoomInfo, Apollo.io, and UpLead are also excellent choices, depending on your size and objectives. ## FAQ

**What are business dataset providers?** Business dataset providers are companies that collect aggregate and deliver structured business information including company profiles contact data firmographic details and market intelligence. These providers offer datasets from sources like LinkedIn Crunchbase job boards and company registries to support B2B sales marketing and research activities.  **How much do business datasets typically cost?** Business dataset pricing varies widely based on data volume, update frequency, and customization. Entry-level options start around $250 for 100,000 records, while enterprise solutions with real-time updates and advanced features can cost several thousand dollars monthly. Most providers offer both pay-as-you-go and subscription models.  **What types of data are included in business datasets?** Business datasets typically include company information (name, industry, size, revenue, location), contact details (emails, phone numbers, job titles), firmographic data (employee count, technology stack, funding), and sometimes behavioral signals like buyer intent data and engagement metrics.  **Which business dataset provider offers the best data quality?** Bright Data leads in data quality with 1B+ verified records from premium sources, rigorous validation processes, and flexible delivery options. ZoomInfo excels for North American coverage with real-time updates and verified contact information, while smaller businesses might prefer Lusha for its user-friendly interface and GDPR compliance.  **How do I choose the right business dataset provider?** Consider your target market (geographic coverage) data requirements (contact types firmographic details) budget constraints integration needs (CRM API capabilities) and compliance requirements (GDPR CCPA). Evaluate data freshness update frequency customization options and customer support quality before committing to a provider.  **Are business datasets GDPR compliant?** Reputable business dataset providers like Bright Data, Lusha, and Cognism ensure GDPR and CCPA compliance through proper consent mechanisms, data processing agreements, and privacy controls. Always verify a provider’s compliance certifications and data sourcing methodologies before purchasing datasets for European markets.  **What is the difference between B2B and B2C datasets?** B2B datasets focus on company information, professional contacts, and business relationships, including firmographic data and decision-maker details. B2C datasets contain consumer information like demographics, purchasing behavior, and personal preferences. B2B data emphasizes business context and professional networks, while B2C prioritizes individual consumer patterns.

## FAQ

**What are social media dataset providers?** Social media dataset providers collect aggregate and deliver structured data from social platforms including user profiles posts engagement metrics follower counts hashtags trends and sentiment data. These providers offer datasets from Facebook Instagram Twitter TikTok LinkedIn and YouTube to support brand monitoring influencer marketing sentiment analysis and market research.  **What types of social media data can I access?** Available data includes user profiles, post content, engagement metrics (likes, shares, comments), follower demographics, hashtag performance, trending topics, influencer statistics, sentiment scores, posting frequency, video views, story metrics, and audience growth patterns. Data varies by platform and provider capabilities.  **How do providers ensure social media data compliance?** Reputable providers like Bright Data comply with GDPR, CCPA, platform APIs, and terms of service through ethical scraping practices, proper authentication, data anonymization, and consent mechanisms. They focus on publicly available data, respect rate limits, and implement privacy controls to ensure legal and ethical data collection.  **What is the difference between social media APIs and dataset providers?** Platform APIs provide limited access to structured data with strict rate limits and access restrictions, often requiring developer accounts. Dataset providers offer comprehensive historical data, unlimited access, pre-processed information, and data from multiple platforms through a single interface, bypassing API limitations and technical complexity.  **How much do social media datasets cost?** Pricing varies from $2.50 per 1,000 records for basic data to custom enterprise pricing based on volume, platforms, and update frequency. Historical datasets support trend analysis, campaign performance tracking, and longitudinal studies. Availability varies by platform—Twitter historical data is more accessible than Instagram or TikTok due to platform restrictions and API changes.

## [Ethical Web Scraping: Guidelines and Best Practices](https://scrapingproxies.best/blog/web-scraping/ethical-web-scraping-guidelines/)

> Web scraping can feel like a superpower. In a few lines of code, you can pull useful information from websites and turn it into insights, products, and resea...

[Web scraping](/glossary/web-scraping/) can feel like a superpower. In a few lines of code, you can pull useful information from websites and turn it into insights, products, and research. Businesses use it to track markets and competitors. Developers use it to power apps and automate workflows. Researchers use it to study trends at scale.

However, scraping is not just a technical task. It’s also a responsibility. The websites you scrape belong to real people and organizations, and your script can affect their performance, costs, and users. Doing it the right way means respecting site rules, staying within legal boundaries, and being careful with personal data. It also means scraping gently so you don’t overload servers or break a service for others.

In this guide, we will walk you through practical, ethics-first habits so you can collect data confidently without causing harm.

## What is Ethical Web Scraping

Ethical web scraping is the practice of collecting data from websites responsibly and respectfully. It involves following the website’s terms of service and robots.txt guidelines, which specify what data can be accessed. Ethical scrapers protect personal information, respect copyright laws, and avoid collecting more data than necessary. They minimize server load by using delays between requests and throttling their scrapers to prevent overwhelming website resources. 

Ethical scraping also means using APIs when available, identifying your scraper with honest user agent strings, and handling errors gracefully. The goal is to gather data while respecting website owners, protecting user privacy, and maintaining a healthy internet ecosystem for everyone.

## Legal Compliance in Web Scraping

Ethics and legality are closely intertwined when it comes to web scraping. Understanding the legal framework not only protects you from potential lawsuits or penalties but also ensures your practices are respectful and responsible.

### **Copyright and Intellectual Property**

In most jurisdictions, raw facts and data are not protected by copyright. However, the way that information is structured, written, or visually presented often is. For example, a list of product prices may not be copyrighted, but a creatively written product description or a unique page layout could be. Copying large portions of text, duplicating a website’s design or layout, or extracting entire sections of content may infringe on copyright or other intellectual property rights.

To avoid legal complications, do not reproduce large amounts of text or replicate visual elements without permission. Instead, focus on extracting the underlying data and using it to generate your own insights, summaries, or visualizations. If you must reference or reuse parts of the content, always attribute the source clearly. Giving credit demonstrates professional integrity and respects content creators’ rights.

### **Privacy Regulations**

Data privacy laws such as the GDPR (Europe) and the CCPA (California) impose strict requirements on how personal information is collected, stored, and used. These laws protect personal information such as names, email addresses, IP addresses, and behavioral data. If your scraping project involves collecting this type of data, you must have a lawful reason—such as consent or contractual need. 

You’re also responsible for informing users how their data will be used and securing it properly. Always store personal data with appropriate safeguards and delete it when no longer needed. Following these rules helps ensure you respect user privacy and avoid legal consequences.

## Checking Website Permissions

Before starting any scraping project, check whether the website allows automated access. This step prevents legal issues and respects the website owner’s wishes.

### **Reading Terms of Service**

Most websites have Terms of Service that outline acceptable use. These terms often address automated data collection directly. Some sites explicitly prohibit scraping, while others may allow it under certain conditions.

Take time to read these terms carefully. If you create an account to access data, you’re agreeing to follow these rules. Violating terms of service can result in account bans, legal action, or worse.

### **Understanding Robots.txt Files**

The robots.txt file is a standard protocol that tells automated bots which parts of a site they can access. You’ll find this file at the root domain (for example, website.com/robots.txt).

This file contains directives for different user agents. Some sections may not be allowed for bots, while others are permitted. Respecting these directives is a fundamental aspect of ethical scraping.

For example, if robots.txt disallows access to a private directory, your scraper should skip those pages. This shows respect for the website owner’s boundaries and demonstrates good faith in your data collection efforts.

## Communicating With Website Owners

When permissions aren’t clear, reaching out directly to website owners can improve data access.

### **Requesting Permission**

A simple email explaining your project and data needs can transform your scraping approach. Many website owners are willing to help if they understand your purpose. They might offer API access, bulk data downloads, or special permissions for research projects.

This direct communication builds trust. It can turn what might have been an adversarial relationship into a collaborative partnership. You’ll often receive higher-quality data through official channels than by scraping.

### **Building Relationships**

Establishing relationships with website owners provides long-term benefits. They might inform you of upcoming changes that could break your scraper. They may even improve their API or data offerings based on your feedback.

These relationships create sustainable data access that benefits both parties. The website owner understands how their data is being used, and you gain reliable access without worrying about bans or blocks.

## Technical Implementation Guidelines

Ethical scraping isn’t just about intent. It’s built into your scraper’s operation. These technical practices minimize disruption and demonstrate respect for website infrastructure.

### **Extracting Only Required Data**

Don’t download entire webpages when you only need specific information. Design your scraper to target exact data elements you need. This approach reduces bandwidth usage, accelerates processing, and conserves server resources.

If you only need product names and prices, don’t download images, reviews, and other unnecessary content. Selective extraction benefits both you and the website you’re scraping.

### **Implementing Request Delays**

Never flood a website with rapid requests. Use delays between requests to avoid overwhelming servers. Even simple pauses of a few seconds can significantly reduce your impact.

Think of your scraper as a polite visitor, not a flood of traffic. Spread your requests over time. This prevents server strain and reduces the chance of triggering security measures.

### **Rate Limiting Your Requests**

Set reasonable limits on how many requests you make within a given timeframe. Most websites can handle normal browsing traffic, but hundreds of requests per second from a single source will cause problems.

Monitor response times and error rates. If you notice the website slowing down or returning errors, reduce your request rate immediately. Adaptive throttling that responds to server conditions shows ethical responsibility.

### **Using APIs When Available**

Many websites offer APIs specifically for data access. APIs provide structured, reliable, and explicitly permitted access to information. When an API exists, use it instead of scraping HTML.

APIs offer several advantages. They have clear usage policies and rate limits. They provide consistent data structure that won’t break when the website design changes. Most importantly, they represent explicit permission from the website owner.

## Identifying Your Scraper Properly

Transparency in web scraping builds trust and provides communication channels if issues arise.

### **Setting Honest User Agents**

Always identify your scraper with a truthful user agent string. This should include information about your bot and contact details for site administrators.

A proper user agent might look like: “ResearchBot/1.0 (research@university.edu)”. This transparency distinguishes your legitimate scraping from malicious bots or attacks.

Website owners appreciate knowing who’s accessing their site. If they have concerns, they can contact you directly rather than immediately blocking your IP address.

### **Maintaining Contact Information**

Include valid contact information in your user agent or make it easily discoverable. This allows website owners to reach you if your scraper causes problems or if they have questions about your data use.

Being reachable demonstrates good faith. It shows you’re willing to address concerns and work cooperatively with site owners.

## Testing Before Scaling

Start small before ramping up to large-scale scraping operations.

### **Beginning With Small Samples**

Always test your scraper on a small number of pages first. Try scraping five to ten pages to verify everything works correctly. This helps you identify bugs, check data quality, and ensure you’re not inadvertently stressing servers.

Only after successful small-scale testing should you increase volume. Gradual scaling allows you to monitor impact and adjust your approach if needed.

### **Monitoring Your Impact**

Track how your scraping affects the websites you’re accessing. Monitor response times; slow responses may indicate server strain. Monitor error rates and patterns that may indicate your scraper is causing issues.

Consider timing your scraping during off-peak hours. Running your scraper at night (local time for the website) typically has less impact than scraping during business hours when legitimate user traffic is highest.

## Handling Errors Responsibly

How your scraper behaves when things go wrong is just as important as its normal operation.

### **Implementing Graceful Failure**

When servers fail to respond or return errors, don’t hammer them with repeated requests. Implement reasonable retry limits, typically three to five attempts maximum.

Use exponential backoff between retries. This means waiting longer after each failed attempt. If the first retry waits two seconds, the second might wait four seconds, the third eight seconds, and so on.

Include circuit breakers that pause all requests if too many errors occur. This prevents your scraper from further stressing an already strained server.

### **Maintaining Comprehensive Logs**

Keep detailed records of your scraping activities. Log which URLs you accessed and when, response codes and errors, the volume of data extracted, and configuration settings for each session.

These logs help you audit your own behavior. They ensure you’re operating within intended parameters and provide transparency if questions arise about your activities.

## Understanding Restricted Websites

Some websites are completely off-limits regardless of technical capability.

### **Healthcare and Financial Data**

Platforms handling personal health records must comply with strict privacy laws such as HIPAA in the United States. Sites hosting financial account data, student records, or government identification systems are protected by legal frameworks and access controls.

Scraping these sites can result in severe legal consequences, including criminal charges, substantial fines, and civil litigation.

### **Protected and Paywalled Content**

Websites serving protected content like academic journals with paywalls, subscription news services, or proprietary research databases require extreme caution. These sites typically employ sophisticated anti-scraping measures.

Circumventing access controls may violate laws like the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act. Instead, seek legitimate access through institutional subscriptions, paid APIs, or formal data-sharing agreements.

### **Social Media Platforms**

Many social media sites prohibit automated scraping in their terms of service due to user privacy concerns. While some data may be publicly visible, the terms of service often explicitly forbid bulk collection.

Always check platform-specific policies before scraping social media. Many platforms offer official APIs for developers that provide legal access to data.

## Avoiding Privacy Violations

Protecting individual privacy is a critical aspect of ethical scraping.

### **Recognizing Personally Identifiable Information**

Personally identifiable information includes any data that can identify a specific individual. Names, email addresses, phone numbers, physical addresses, and social security numbers all qualify as PII.

Even combinations of non-sensitive data can become PII. For example, a zip code combined with a birthdate might identify someone uniquely in a small area.

### **Using Common Sense**

You might encounter websites that inadvertently display private or protected data publicly. If you scrape en masse without considering the actual information, you could end up with sensitive data you shouldn’t have.

Always review what you’re collecting. Ask yourself whether individuals would expect this data to be harvested and used. When in doubt, err on the side of caution.

## Building Maintainable Code

Ethical scraping includes writing clean, transparent code that’s easy to audit and update.

### **Creating Clear Documentation**

Structure your code with descriptive functions and variable names that explain their purpose. Include comments explaining each component’s role. Separate concerns like networking, parsing, and data storage into distinct modules.

This organization makes your scraper easier to maintain in accordance with ethical standards. It also helps identify potential issues before they impact websites.

### **Regular Code Reviews**

Schedule regular reviews of your scraping code and activities. The web ecosystem constantly evolves with changing technologies, policies, and legal frameworks.

What was acceptable last year might not be today. Don’t assume you still have permission just because you did previously. Stay informed about best practices and update your approach accordingly.

## Managing Concurrent Requests

Parallel scraping can be powerful but potentially harmful if not controlled properly.

### **Setting Connection Limits**

When handling concurrent requests, set reasonable limits on the number of simultaneous connections. Usually, two to five concurrent connections is appropriate for most websites.

More connections might seem efficient, but they can overwhelm servers. Remember that other users are also accessing the site. Your scraper should be one polite visitor among many, not a dominant force.

### **Implementing Adaptive Throttling**

Monitor how the website responds to your requests. If response times slow or errors increase, reduce your rate automatically. This adaptive approach respects server capacity and prevents issues before they escalate.

## Understanding Fair Use and Attribution

When using scraped data, consider how your use affects original creators.

### **Providing Proper Attribution**

When you publish work based on scraped data, credit the sources appropriately. This shows integrity and builds trust with content creators and your audience.

Attribution doesn’t just mean listing sources. Consider how your use might impact the original creator’s work. Are you providing value, or simply repackaging their content?

### **Avoiding Derivative Works**

While facts aren’t copyrighted, creative presentations of those facts may be. Creating derivative works that closely mirror original content can violate intellectual property rights.

Transform the data meaningfully. Add analysis, combine multiple sources, or present information in genuinely new ways that provide distinct value.

## The Long-Term Benefits of Ethical Scraping

Ethical web scraping creates sustainable value for your projects and the broader data community.

### **Avoiding Blocks and Bans**

When you scrape ethically, you’re less likely to be blocked or banned. This means more stable data sources and predictable results. You’ll save time and resources that would otherwise be spent circumventing blocks or rebuilding scrapers.

### **Building Collaborative Relationships**

Website owners who recognize your considerate approach may provide formal access or partnerships. These collaborative relationships often result in higher-quality data and more sustainable access than aggressive scraping could ever achieve.

### **Contributing to a Healthier Internet**

Ethical scrapers contribute to a web ecosystem where data collection coexists with website sustainability. Your respectful practices help ensure that valuable online resources remain available for everyone.

## Final Words

Ethical web scraping is about striking a balance between gathering the data you need and respecting the rights of website owners, their users, and applicable legal guidelines. Just because you have the technical ability to scrape doesn’t mean you’re authorized to do so. Always think carefully about the ethical implications before you start.

Ensure you have clear permissions, use respectful technical practices, and handle errors in a way that doesn’t harm the site. Be transparent about your actions and keep the process open and honest. Ethical scraping isn’t just about following rules—it’s about being a responsible part of the internet. By doing so, you help maintain a healthy digital ecosystem where data collection can coexist with website needs.

## FAQ

**Is web scraping legal?** Web scraping public data is generally legal in the US following the hiQ v. LinkedIn ruling. However legality depends on what data you scrape and how you use it and whether you violate terms of service. Scraping copyrighted content or personal data requires careful legal consideration.  **What is robots.txt and should I follow it?** Robots.txt is a file that tells web crawlers which pages to avoid. While not legally binding following robots.txt demonstrates good faith and ethical intent. Ignoring it may expose you to legal risk and indicates disregard for website owner preferences.  **How do I scrape ethically without overloading servers?** Implement rate limiting with 1-5 second delays between requests. Respect server resources by scraping during off-peak hours and limiting concurrent connections. Monitor response times and back off if the server slows down significantly.  **What data should I avoid scraping?** Avoid scraping personal identifiable information (PII) and copyrighted content and data behind login walls and content explicitly prohibited in robots.txt or terms of service. When in doubt consult legal counsel before scraping sensitive data.  **Do I need to identify my web scraper?** Yes. Use a descriptive User-Agent string that identifies your bot and includes contact information.
