## FAQ

**What is a Substack scraper?** A Substack scraper is a tool that extracts newsletter content, author profiles, publication metadata, and engagement statistics from Substack.com. It captures article text, subscriber estimates, comment counts, like metrics, publication frequency, and author analytics for competitive research, trend analysis, and newsletter market intelligence.  **Can Substack scrapers access paid newsletters?** No—scrapers cannot bypass Substack’s paywall without valid subscriber credentials. Public scrapers access: free posts, post previews, public author bios, publication descriptions, and visible subscriber counts. To scrape paid-only content: authenticate with subscriber cookies (violates ToS) or use Substack’s official API (requires author permission, RSS feeds for public posts only).  **Which Substack scraper is most reliable?** Apify’s Substack scraper handles pagination and article extraction reliably. Bright Data offers Substack-specific collectors. For custom scraping: [BeautifulSoup](https://scrapingproxies.best/blog/web-scraping/beautifulsoup-web-scraping/) works well since Substack uses server-side rendering (no JavaScript rendering needed). Substack’s clean HTML structure makes parsing easier than Medium—success rates 95%+ with proper rate limiting.  **What data can I extract from Substack publications?** Extract: post title, subtitle, author name, publication name, publish date, post content (text + images), subscriber count estimates, like counts, comment counts, post categories/tags, author bio, publication description, social links, RSS feed URL, custom domain info. Note: exact subscriber numbers often hidden; estimates based on engagement metrics.  **How to scrape multiple Substack newsletters?** Use publication list URLs (substack.com/browse) or curated lists to discover newsletters. Extract publication URLs, then iterate through each publication’s /archive page to list all posts. For each post: extract metadata and full content. Rate limit: 1 request/2 seconds per publication. For 100+ newsletters: use IP rotation and distribute across 5-10 proxies.  **Is Substack easier to scrape than Medium?** Yes—Substack advantages: server-side rendered HTML (no headless browser needed), simpler DOM structure, no paywall for most content, more lenient rate limiting, fewer anti-bot measures. Medium challenges: heavy JavaScript, stricter rate limits, larger paywall coverage, sophisticated bot detection. Substack scraping success rates: 95%+ vs Medium’s 80-85%.  **Which tool handles Substack RSS feeds?** All Substack publications provide RSS feeds (publicationname.substack.com/feed). Use RSS parsers (feedparser in Python, rss-parser in Node.js) for automated content monitoring—no scraping needed. RSS includes: recent posts, titles, summaries, publish dates. Limitation: RSS only shows last 10-20 posts; scrape /archive for complete history.

## FAQ

**What is an Etsy scraper?** An Etsy scraper is a tool that automatically extracts product data from Etsy.com including titles, prices, descriptions, images, reviews, seller information, and sales metrics. It converts unstructured HTML into structured data (CSV, JSON) for market research, competitor analysis, pricing intelligence, and dropshipping product sourcing.  **Which Etsy scraper is easiest to use?** Bright Data’s Web Scraper IDE and Apify offer point-and-click Etsy scrapers requiring zero coding. Octoparse provides visual workflow builder for Etsy. For developers: Scrapy with custom spiders or Beautiful Soup. No-code tools cost $50-200/month; developer tools are free but require 2-5 hours setup time.  **Is scraping Etsy legal?** Scraping publicly visible Etsy data (product listings, prices, reviews) falls in a legal gray area. Etsy’s Terms of Service prohibit automated access, but US courts generally allow scraping public data for research/analysis. Best practices: respect robots.txt, use rate limiting (1-2 requests/second), don’t access private seller data, and consult legal counsel for commercial use.  **What data can I extract from Etsy?** Extract: product title, price, description, images, category, tags, materials, shipping info, seller name/location, shop reviews, product reviews/ratings, favorites count, listing views, sales estimates, last updated date. Advanced scrapers also capture: shop policies, about sections, social links, and historical pricing data for trend analysis.  **Do I need proxies for Etsy scraping?** Yes—Etsy implements rate limiting and IP blocking for automated traffic. Use residential proxies (not datacenter) for 95%+ success rates. Rotate IPs every 10-20 requests, maintain 2-3 second delays between requests, and use realistic user agents. Quality Etsy scrapers include built-in proxy rotation—expect $3-8/GB for residential IPs.  **How fast can I scrape Etsy listings?** Conservative rate: 1-2 requests per second per IP (3600-7200 listings/hour). Aggressive with proxy rotation: 5-10 requests/second (18,000-36,000 listings/hour). Etsy monitors velocity—stay under 10,000 listings/day per IP to avoid blocks. Use distributed scraping with 10-20 IPs for large-scale extraction while maintaining per-IP limits.  **Which Etsy scraper handles pagination best?** Apify’s Etsy scraper automatically handles infinite scroll and pagination. Bright Data’s collector manages page navigation via visual selector. For custom scrapers: Selenium/Playwright handle dynamic loading; Scrapy with scrapy-playwright for JavaScript rendering. All should implement exponential backoff for rate limit errors (HTTP 429) and retry failed pages 2-3 times.

## FAQ

**Does Pinterest have an official API?** Pinterest offers an official API primarily for business partners and advertisers. It provides access to pin creation and board management but not bulk data extraction. For scraping pins and images at scale third-party scraper tools are the practical solution.  **Is scraping Pinterest legal?** Scraping publicly available Pinterest data is generally legal but may violate Pinterest Terms of Service. Use scraped data responsibly for legitimate purposes like market research and competitive intelligence. Avoid scraping private content and respect rate limits.  **What data can I extract from Pinterest?** Pinterest scrapers can extract pins (images and descriptions and URLs and engagement metrics) and boards (names and pin counts and followers) and user profiles. Premium tools also extract related pins and trending content for comprehensive analysis.  **Which Pinterest scraper works with Python?** Several options work with Python: Apify Pinterest Scraper offers a Python API client and Bright Data provides Python SDK integration. Most commercial scrapers also provide REST APIs that work with Python requests library.  **How do I avoid getting blocked when scraping Pinterest?** Use rotating residential proxies to distribute requests across different IPs and implement delays between requests (2-5 seconds minimum). Premium scraping tools like Bright Data handle anti-bot bypass automatically.  **What is the best free Pinterest scraper?** Apify offers a free tier with limited monthly credits for their Pinterest Scraper. Open-source Python libraries provide basic scraping capabilities but require proxy management. For serious data collection paid tools offer better reliability.  **How much does Pinterest scraping cost?** Pricing varies by provider: Apify charges based on compute units ($5-50/month) and Bright Data offers pay-per-request pricing ($0.001-0.01 per request). Dedicated scraping services range $100-500/month with proxy infrastructure included.

## 7. Custom Python + Playwright Stack

A custom Node.js and Puppeteer setup gives you full control over scraping Mercado Libre. Puppeteer runs headless Chrome, allowing pages to load and execute scripts just like a regular browser. This environment is ideal for JavaScript developers, as it integrates smoothly with backend or frontend tools. You can automate actions like scrolling, clicking, and navigating to product details. The entire stack can be run in containers, virtual machines, or serverless functions, giving you flexibility in deployment. You have control over proxies, logging, and monitoring, making it easy to customize. This approach is perfect for teams that prefer working with JavaScript and want a high level of control.

### Key features:

- **Full browser automation:** Playwright controls Chromium, Firefox, or WebKit for real rendering.

- **Fine control over logic:** You define how pages load, scroll, and click.

- **Custom parsing:** Use libraries like BeautifulSoup or lxml for flexible HTML parsing.

- **Modular design:** You can plug in your own logging, retries, and storage.

- **Integration with proxies:** Combine with residential or [datacenter proxies](https://scrapingproxies.best/datacenter-proxies/) for better stability.

- **Open-source tooling:** No license fees for the core libraries.

### Pros:

- Maximum flexibility and control

- No vendor lock-in for scraping logic

- Great for very custom workflows

- Can be tightly integrated with your internal systems

### Cons:

- Requires development and maintenance time

- You must handle scaling, retries, and monitoring yourself

- You need to manage proxy providers separately

### Pricing:

Depends on infrastructure and proxies. It can start on a small VPS or cloud instance, along with a proxy plan.

This stack works well for developers who are familiar with JavaScript and want complete control over the scraping process. You can run it on your own servers, virtual machines, or serverless platforms. It’s perfect for teams that need flexibility and want to customize their scraping setup for complex needs.

### Cons:

## FAQ

**Does Mercado Libre have an official API?** Mercado Libre offers a comprehensive official API for registered developers and sellers providing access to products and orders and questions. However the API has strict rate limits. For large-scale competitive analysis third-party scrapers offer more flexibility.  **What data can I extract from Mercado Libre?** Mercado Libre scrapers extract product listings (titles and prices and images) and seller profiles (ratings and sales history) and customer reviews and shipping information. Advanced tools capture data across multiple country domains.  **Which countries does Mercado Libre operate in?** Mercado Libre operates across 18 Latin American countries including Argentina (MLA) and Brazil (MLB) and Mexico (MLM) and Chile (MLC) and Colombia (MCO) and Peru (MPE). Each country has a separate domain with localized content.  **How do I handle Mercado Libre rate limits?** Use rotating residential proxies from Latin American countries and implement request delays (3-5 seconds) and distribute scraping across multiple sessions. Premium tools like Bright Data handle rate limiting automatically.  **Is Mercado Libre data available in English?** Mercado Libre content is primarily in Spanish (most countries) and Portuguese (Brazil). Scraped data reflects the original language. Some scraper tools offer built-in translation or you can use translation APIs post-extraction.  **What proxies work best for Mercado Libre?** Residential proxies from Argentina and Brazil and Mexico and other target countries perform best. Datacenter proxies often trigger CAPTCHAs. Bright Data and Oxylabs offer Latin American residential IPs.  **How much does Mercado Libre scraping cost?** Apify charges $5-30/month for moderate Mercado Libre scraping. Bright Data offers pay-per-request pricing at $0.001-0.005 per product page. Dedicated Latin American e-commerce scraping services range $150-500/month.

## FAQ

**Does G2 have an official API?** G2 offers an official API for verified vendors and enterprise partners providing access to reviews and ratings. However API access requires approval and carries significant costs ($10000+/year). Third-party G2 scrapers are more accessible.  **What data can I extract from G2?** G2 scrapers extract software reviews (ratings and pros/cons and use cases) and reviewer profiles (company size and industry and role) and product comparisons and category rankings and pricing information and feature lists.  **Is scraping G2 legal?** Scraping publicly available G2 reviews is generally legal but violates G2 Terms of Service. G2 actively blocks scrapers using CAPTCHAs and IP detection. Use scraped data for legitimate competitive intelligence purposes only.  **How do I avoid getting blocked on G2?** G2 has aggressive anti-bot protection. Use [residential proxies](https://scrapingproxies.best/residential-proxies/) (datacenter IPs are quickly blocked) and implement human-like delays (5-10 seconds) and rotate user agents. Premium scrapers like Bright Data offer specialized G2 extraction.  **Can I scrape G2 competitor comparisons?** Yes G2 scrapers can extract head-to-head comparison pages showing how products stack against competitors including ratings breakdowns and feature comparisons and user preferences. This data is valuable for competitive positioning.  **What is the best free G2 scraper?** Apify offers a G2 Scraper with free tier credits (limited monthly usage). Open-source Python solutions exist but require significant proxy investment to work reliably. For consistent G2 data extraction paid tools are practically necessary.  **How much does G2 scraping cost?** Third-party G2 scrapers range $50-200/month for moderate volume. Bright Data charges $0.01-0.02 per successful G2 page due to high anti-bot complexity. G2 official API starts at $10000+/year for enterprise access.

## FAQ

**Does Quora have an official API?** Quora deprecated its official API in 2018 and no longer provides public API access for data extraction. The only official integration is through Quora Ads API for advertisers. Third-party scraper tools are the only practical solution.  **What data can I extract from Quora?** Quora scrapers extract questions (text and topics and view counts) and answers (content and upvotes and author info and timestamps) and user profiles (credentials and follower counts) and topics and spaces and comment threads.  **Is scraping Quora legal?** Scraping publicly available Quora content is generally legal but violates Quora Terms of Service. Use scraped data for legitimate purposes like content research and trend analysis. Never republish answers verbatim or scrape private content.  **How do I scrape Quora without getting blocked?** Quora has moderate anti-bot protection. Use residential proxies (datacenter IPs get blocked quickly) and implement delays between requests (3-5 seconds) and rotate user agents. Premium tools handle anti-detection automatically.  **What is the best Quora scraper for Python?** Apify Quora Scraper offers Python API integration. The open-source quora-scraper library on PyPI provides basic extraction capabilities. For production use combine requests with rotating proxies or use Bright Data Python SDK.  **Can I scrape Quora Spaces and Topics?** Yes Quora scrapers can extract Space content (posts and members and discussions) and Topic pages (questions and followers and related topics). This data is valuable for identifying trending subjects and finding content ideas.  **How much does Quora scraping cost?** Apify charges $5-25/month for moderate Quora scraping volume. Bright Data offers pay-per-request pricing at $0.002-0.005 per page. Budget $50-150/month for reliable ongoing Quora data extraction with anti-detection features.

## [Web Scraping with Perplexity](https://scrapingproxies.best/blog/web-scraping/web-scraping-with-perplexity/)

> TL;DR Perplexity&nbsp;is an AI-powered research assistant that reads, summarizes, and synthesizes information from multiple web sources—no coding required. I...

## TL;DR

- **Perplexity** is an AI-powered research assistant that reads, summarizes, and synthesizes information from multiple web sources—no coding required.

- It’s perfect for **quick research, price comparisons, trend analysis, and exploratory data gathering**.

- It’s **not a traditional web scraper**—you won’t get structured CSV files or scheduled automated extraction.

- For **large-scale, repeatable, structured datasets**, traditional scraping tools or APIs are still the way to go.

- Always **respect Terms of Service, robots.txt, and privacy laws** when gathering web data.

## Introduction

Ever feel like the information you need is hiding all over the internet? We get it. Whether it’s prices, reviews, or the latest updates, it can be a pain to dig through dozens of websites just to find what you’re looking for.

That’s where **web scraping** comes in—it helps you collect data from multiple pages quickly and efficiently. And now, with powerful AI tools like **Perplexity**, you don’t need to be a tech expert to gather insights from the web.

In this guide, we’ll explain what web scraping really is, how Perplexity makes web research easier, when it can replace traditional scraping, and when you’ll still need code-based tools. Whether you’re a student, researcher, small business owner, or just a curious mind, this is the perfect place to start.

## What Is Web Scraping (Really)?

Web scraping is the automated process of extracting structured data from websites. Instead of manually copying and pasting information page by page, a scraper program visits web pages, identifies the data you want (like prices, reviews, or product names), and saves it in a structured format like CSV, JSON, or a database.

### Example: Manual vs. Automated Scraping

Let’s say you want to compare smartphone prices across five e-commerce sites.

- **Manual way**: Open each site, search for the phone, copy the price, paste it into a spreadsheet. Repeat 50 times. Slow and painful!

- **Automated scraping**: A program visits all five sites, extracts prices in seconds, and saves them neatly in a table.

It’s like having a research assistant that never sleeps.

### Traditional Web Scraping Tools

Classic scraping requires programming knowledge and tools like:

- **Python libraries**: BeautifulSoup, Scrapy, Selenium

- **Browser automation**: Playwright, Puppeteer

- **Proxy and unblocking tools**: To handle anti-bot systems and IP blocks

These tools are powerful, but they have a learning curve.

## How Perplexity Helps with Web Research

**Perplexity** is an AI-powered search and research assistant. It doesn’t “scrape” websites in the traditional sense—it **reads, understands, and synthesizes information** from multiple sources, then presents you with a clean summary and citations.

Think of it as a smart research assistant that:

- Reads and summarizes websites

- Provides answers from multiple sources with citations

- Pulls near real-time data using its browsing mode

- Understands context and sentiment behind text

This means you can gather insights from the web without writing a single line of code.

Let’s explore how Perplexity can handle web research tasks that feel like scraping.

## 5 Ways Perplexity Simplifies Web Research

### 1. Instant Data Summaries

Perplexity doesn’t just show you a list of links. It reads those links and gives you a clean summary with sources.

**Example**: You ask, *“What are the latest iPhone 15 prices around the world?”*

Perplexity will:

- Find recent data from e-commerce websites

- Summarize the prices by region

- Present them in an easy-to-read format with source links

You don’t need to visit ten websites. The tool already did the legwork for you.

### 2. Near Real-Time Research

One challenge with web data is staying up to date. Prices, news, and reviews change daily—sometimes hourly.

Perplexity can pull data from the latest pages using its **browsing mode**. It scans current web pages, extracts key facts, and presents the most relevant information.

**This is extremely helpful if you’re tracking**:

- News headlines

- Stock prices

- Product launches

- Sports scores

- Trending topics on social media

You don’t need to build a scraper or schedule refreshes. Just ask a smart question and get fresh insights.

**Note**: Results depend on source availability and crawl frequency. Some pages may have slight delays or may not be accessible due to paywalls or login requirements.

### 3. Natural Language Questions (No Code Needed)

With traditional web scraping, you’d need to write code like this:

<code>from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import requests

url = "https://example.com/products"
response = requests.get(url)
soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, "html.parser")
prices = soup.find_all("span", class_="price")

for price in prices:
    print(price.text)

Not fun for non-coders.

But with Perplexity, you just ask:

**“What are the top trending laptops under $1000?”**

Boom! The tool does the heavy lifting—visits sites, reads the content, compares the data, and summarizes the best options with links.

### 4. Reduced Setup, Not Zero Blocking Risk

Many websites block traditional scrapers. They detect bots and stop them from accessing data using techniques like CAPTCHA, rate limiting, or IP blocking.

Perplexity can browse like a user, which often reduces the effort needed to gather information. However, **some sites still restrict automated access** through:

- Paywalls

- Login gates

- Anti-bot systems

- robots.txt restrictions

**Important**: Always respect **Terms of Service** and **robots.txt** rules. Even AI-powered tools must comply with a site’s access policies and applicable privacy laws (like GDPR or CCPA).

### 5. Better Context and Understanding

Let’s say you’re researching product reviews. A traditional scraper just grabs text—it doesn’t know if a review is positive or negative.

Perplexity’s AI can **understand sentiment**.

It knows when people say, *“This laptop is amazing!”* or *“Battery life is disappointing.”*

That means **better insights**, not just raw data. You get analysis, not just extraction.

## When to Use Perplexity vs. Traditional Scraping vs. APIs

Not sure which tool to use? Here’s a quick comparison:

### ✅ **Use Perplexity for**:

- Quick discovery and exploratory research

- Cross-source synthesis and summarization

- Comparing products, prices, or features

- Follow-up Q&A and iterative research

- Compiling short lists with citations

- Sentiment analysis and context understanding

### ✅ **Use Traditional Scrapers for**:

- Large-scale, repeatable data collection

- Structured datasets (CSV, JSON, SQL)

- Scheduled or automated scraping (e.g., every hour)

- Field-level accuracy and schema control

- Deterministic, auditable pipelines

- Long-term data archiving and versioning

### ✅ **Use First-Party APIs for**:

- Official, reliable access to data

- Stable schemas and documentation

- Compliance and legal clarity

- Rate-limited but guaranteed uptime

## Step-by-Step: How to Use Perplexity for Your Data Needs

Let’s say you run a small business and want to **monitor competitor prices**. Here’s how you could do it with Perplexity:

### Workflow

- **Open Perplexity.ai**

- **Ask a specific question**: *“What are the current prices of [Product Name] on Amazon, Walmart, and Best Buy? Include currency and URLs.”*

- **Review the summary with sources**

- **Click on source links** to verify accuracy

- **Copy the results** or take a screenshot for your records

- **Track changes over time** by asking follow-up questions

### Pro Tips: Prompt Templates You Can Copy

Use these templates to get better, more structured results:

**Price Comparison**:

“Summarize current prices for ‘iPhone 15 128GB’ from Amazon, Walmart, and Best Buy. Return a table with columns: retailer, price, currency, URL. Include 3 sources and note the timestamp.”

**Product Research**:

“Extract the top 10 laptops under $1000 with model name, CPU, RAM, screen size, price, and source link. Note data freshness and any uncertainty.”

**Review Sentiment**:

“What are customers saying about [Product Name] on Reddit and Amazon? Summarize the top 5 positive and negative themes with examples.”

**Trending Topics**:

“What are the trending AI tools this week? Include links, short descriptions, and why they’re popular.”

## Tips to Get Better Results with Perplexity

To make the most of Perplexity, follow these best practices:

✅ **Be specific**: The clearer your question, the better the answer. Include details like price range, region, or time frame.

✅ **Mention sources**: Want data from Reddit, Twitter, Amazon, or specific blogs? Say so in your prompt.

✅ **Use follow-ups**: Perplexity remembers your conversation thread. You can ask clarifying or deeper questions.

✅ **Compare items**: Ask it to compare products, prices, features, or opinions side by side.

✅ **Verify key data**: Open 2–3 cited sources and confirm critical fields like prices or specs. Capture timestamps for your records.

✅ **Export manually**: Copy results into a spreadsheet or note-taking app. Perplexity doesn’t auto-export to CSV (yet).

✅ **Stay updated**: Use it regularly for fresh insights. Data freshness depends on source availability and crawl timing.

## Data Quality and Verification Checklist

AI tools like Perplexity are powerful, but they can sometimes introduce errors or “hallucinate” information. Here’s how to ensure quality:

- **Define your schema**: What fields do you need? (e.g., product name, price, currency, URL, date)

- **Verify primary sources**: Click through to the original pages and confirm key data points

- **Normalize units**: Convert currencies, weights, or measurements to a common standard

- **Capture timestamps**: Note when the data was retrieved

- **Document your prompts**: Save your questions and responses for reproducibility

- **Deduplicate results**: Remove duplicate entries by SKU, URL, or title

## Legal and Ethical Considerations

Before you start gathering web data—whether with Perplexity, scrapers, or APIs—keep these guidelines in mind:

### ✅ Respect Terms of Service

- Read and follow the **Terms of Service** of the websites you’re researching

- Many sites explicitly prohibit automated data collection

### ✅ Check robots.txt

- The robots.txt file tells you which pages a site allows bots to access

- Example: https://example.com/robots.txt

### ✅ Avoid Overloading Servers

- Don’t send too many requests too quickly (rate limiting)

- Be a good web citizen

### ✅ Respect Privacy Laws

- **GDPR** (Europe), **CCPA** (California), and other privacy laws regulate the collection and use of personal data

- Avoid collecting personally identifiable information (PII) without consent

### ✅ Attribute Sources

- Always cite and link to your sources

- Don’t misrepresent AI-generated summaries as your own original research

### ✅ Avoid Bypassing Access Controls

- Don’t bypass paywalls, login gates, or technical restrictions

- If content is behind authentication, get permission or subscribe

## When You Outgrow Perplexity: Scaling to Structured Scraping

Perplexity is fantastic for discovery and synthesis. But what if you need:

- **Thousands of records** updated daily?

- **Structured JSON or CSV exports**?

- **Scheduled, automated pipelines**?

- **Integration with databases or BI tools**?

That’s when you’ll want to use traditional scraping tools or APIs.

### Example: Structured Scraping with Code

Here’s a quick example using Python and Playwright for a JavaScript-heavy site:

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as p:
browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=True)
page = browser.new_page()
page.goto("https://example.com/products")

# Wait for dynamic content to load
page.wait_for_selector(".product-card")

# Extract structured data
products = page.query_selector_all(".product-card")
for product in products:
    name = product.query_selector(".product-name").inner_text()
    price = product.query_selector(".product-price").inner_text()
    print(f"{name}: {price}")

browser.close()

This gives you full control over selectors, pagination, retries, and output format.

## Conclusion

Web scraping is evolving, and it’s no longer limited to developers writing complex code or running bots. With powerful AI tools like **Perplexity**, anyone can access, explore, and interpret web data without needing technical skills.

Acting as an intelligent research assistant, Perplexity simplifies the process—just ask a question, and it delivers relevant, near real-time information with citations. Instead of relying on time-consuming scraping scripts for quick research, you can now get the insights you need quickly and effortlessly.

But remember: **Perplexity is a research tool, not a replacement for structured, large-scale data extraction**. When you need thousands of records, scheduled pipelines, or CSV exports, traditional scraping tools and APIs are still your best bet.

As web intelligence becomes more accessible, tools like Perplexity are redefining how we gather and use information online—making data-driven decisions easier for everyone, from students to enterprise teams.

## FAQs

**What is Perplexity?** Perplexity is an AI-powered search tool that combines real-time browsing with natural language understanding to summarize answers from across the web — no coding needed.  **Can Perplexity be used for web scraping?** Yes, it can. While it doesn’t replace traditional scraping tools for large datasets, it’s great for collecting and summarizing web data in real time using simple questions.  **Do I need technical skills to use Perplexity for scraping?** Not at all. ## FAQ

**What is a SERP API?** A SERP API (Search Engine Results Page API) extracts search results from Google and other engines programmatically. It returns structured JSON data including organic rankings, featured snippets, ads, People Also Ask boxes, and local pack results—essential for SEO tools, rank trackers, and competitive analysis.  **Which SERP API is cheapest?** SerpApi offers 100 free searches/month. DataForSEO provides the lowest per-request pricing at $0.0006 with volume discounts. ValueSERP charges $0.002 per search. Budget providers cost $50-100/month for 10K-50K requests, while enterprise solutions (Bright Data, Oxylabs) start at $500+/month.  **Do I need proxies with SERP APIs?** No—quality SERP APIs include proxy rotation, CAPTCHA solving, and IP management automatically. This is their core value over DIY scraping. Premium providers use [residential proxies](https://scrapingproxies.best/residential-proxies/) for 99%+ success rates. Budget APIs may have lower reliability without robust proxy infrastructure.  **Can I get real-time Google search results?** Yes—all major SERP APIs provide real-time results updated within seconds. Configure location targeting (country, state, city), device type (mobile/desktop), and language settings to get localized results. Note that Google personalizes results, so identical queries may return different rankings.  **Which SERP API has the best Python support?** SerpApi has the most comprehensive Python library with detailed documentation. ScraperAPI and DataForSEO offer robust Python SDKs. Most APIs provide REST endpoints that work with the standard requests library—basic implementation takes 10-20 lines of code regardless of provider.  **Are SERP APIs legal to use?** Yes, SERP APIs are legal tools. However, scraping may violate Google’s Terms of Service. Legitimate use cases include SEO monitoring, rank tracking, competitive research, and market analysis. Avoid excessive requests, respect rate limits, and don’t use data for spam or manipulation.  **What’s better: a SERP API or building a custom scraper?** SERP APIs save 100+ development hours, handle anti-bot measures automatically, provide structured data, and include ongoing maintenance. Custom scrapers cost $50-200/hour to build, require constant updates when search engines change, and need proxy management. APIs are more cost-effective unless processing 1M+ monthly searches.

## FAQ

**What is a SERP API?** A SERP API (Search Engine Results Page API) allows developers to programmatically extract search results from Google, Bing, or other search engines without manual scraping. It returns structured JSON data including rankings, featured snippets, ads, and related searches—essential for SEO tools, rank trackers, and competitive analysis.  **Which SERP API is cheapest?** SerpApi offers a free tier (100 searches/month), followed by DataForSEO ($0.0006 per request with 100K+ volume discounts) and ValueSERP ($0.002 per search). Bright Data and Oxylabs are premium ($500-1500/month minimum) but include proxies and higher success rates for enterprise needs.  **Do I need proxies with SERP APIs?** No—quality SERP APIs handle proxy rotation, CAPTCHA solving, and IP management automatically. This is their main value vs DIY scraping. Premium providers (Bright Data, Oxylabs) use [residential](https://scrapingproxies.best/residential-proxies/) IPs for 99%+ success rates. Budget APIs may have lower reliability without proper proxy infrastructure.  **Can I get real-time Google search results?** Yes—all major SERP APIs provide real-time results (updated within seconds). However, Google’s personalization means results vary by location, device, and search history. Use location targeting parameters (city, state, country) and device type settings (mobile/desktop) for accurate data.  **Which SERP API has best Python support?** SerpApi has the most comprehensive Python library with excellent documentation. ScraperAPI and DataForSEO also offer robust Python SDKs. Most APIs provide REST endpoints that work with standard requests library—implementation takes 10-20 lines of code regardless of provider.  **Are SERP APIs legal to use?** Yes, when used responsibly. SERP APIs don’t violate laws, but may breach search engine Terms of Service. Use cases like SEO monitoring, competitive research, and market analysis are widely accepted. Avoid excessive requests, respect robots.txt, and don’t use data for prohibited purposes (spam, manipulation).  **What’s better: SERP API or custom scraper?** SERP APIs save 100+ hours of development, handle anti-bot measures automatically, provide structured data formats, and include maintenance/updates. Custom scrapers cost $50-200/hour to build, require constant maintenance when search engines change, and need proxy management. APIs cost less unless you’re processing 1M+ searches monthly.

## FAQ

**Does DuckDuckGo have an official search API?** DuckDuckGo offers the Instant Answer API for accessing structured data like definitions, calculations, and quick facts—but no official API for full web search results. For complete search data extraction, third-party providers like SerpApi, DataForSEO, and ScraperAPI offer DuckDuckGo scraping solutions.  **Is DuckDuckGo API free?** The official Instant Answer API is free with reasonable rate limits. Third-party search APIs for DuckDuckGo results typically cost $0.002-$0.01 per request. SerpApi includes DuckDuckGo in its free tier (100 searches/month). Budget options start at $50/month for dedicated DuckDuckGo scraping.  **Why use DuckDuckGo instead of Google for search data?** DuckDuckGo doesn’t track users or personalize results, providing consistent, unbiased search data ideal for research and competitive analysis. Lower competition for API access means better success rates and cheaper pricing. Privacy-conscious users and applications benefit from DuckDuckGo’s no-tracking policy.  **What’s the DuckDuckGo Instant Answer API?** The Instant Answer API returns structured data for queries including definitions, calculations, conversions, and facts sourced from DuckDuckGo’s Instant Answers. It’s free to use, returns JSON responses, and is ideal for building quick-answer features—but doesn’t return full web search results.  **How do I scrape DuckDuckGo search results?** Use third-party SERP APIs that support DuckDuckGo (SerpApi, DataForSEO, ScraperAPI). They handle proxy rotation and parsing automatically. Alternatively, use Python libraries like duckduckgo-search for basic scraping—but be mindful of rate limits and terms of service compliance.  **What are DuckDuckGo API rate limits?** The Instant Answer API has no published limits but expects reasonable usage. Third-party providers typically allow 50-100 requests/second with volume-based pricing. For high-volume scraping, dedicated DuckDuckGo API plans offer higher limits without throttling.  **Can I use DuckDuckGo API for commercial projects?** The Instant Answer API permits commercial use with attribution requirements. Third-party scraping APIs allow commercial use under their terms. Always review specific provider policies for data resale, storage limits, and acceptable use cases before implementing in production applications.

## FAQ

**What is Bing Search API?** Bing Search API allows developers to programmatically access Microsoft Bing search results. It returns web pages, images, videos, news, and related searches in structured JSON format—ideal for building search features, SEO tools, and AI applications without manual scraping.  **Is Bing Search API free?** Microsoft offers a free tier with 1,000 transactions per month through Azure. Third-party providers like SerpApi and DataForSEO also offer free tiers (100-500 requests/month). Paid plans start at $0.003-$0.01 per request depending on volume and provider.  **How do I get a Bing Search API key?** Create a Microsoft Azure account and navigate to Cognitive Services. Add a Bing Search resource to generate your API key. For third-party providers, sign up on their platform and access keys from your dashboard—most provide instant key generation.  **What’s the difference between Bing Web Search API and Bing Custom Search API?** Bing Web Search API returns standard Bing search results across the entire web. Bing Custom Search API lets you define specific websites to search within, creating a branded search experience limited to domains you configure—ideal for site search implementations.  **Which Bing Search API is best for Python developers?** Azure Bing Search works well with the requests library (10-15 lines of code). SerpApi offers a dedicated Python package with excellent documentation. DataForSEO provides comprehensive SDKs. All return JSON responses compatible with standard Python data handling.  **What are Bing Search API rate limits?** Azure’s free tier allows 3 transactions per second and 1,000 per month. Paid tiers vary: S1 offers 250 TPS, S9 provides 1,000 TPS. Third-party APIs typically have higher limits (50-100 requests/second) with volume-based pricing.  **Why use a third-party Bing API provider instead of Azure directly?** Third-party providers offer simpler pricing (pay-per-request vs Azure subscriptions), built-in proxy rotation, CAPTCHA handling, and unified APIs for multiple search engines. They’re ideal for scraping use cases where Azure’s Terms of Service restrictions apply.

## [](#Market-Trends-amp-Insights)Market Trends & Insights

Now, let’s try and understand how the changes in the industry and the new use cases are affecting the demand for the different proxy types.

### [](#The-AI-Data-Revolution)The AI Data Revolution

After seeing some other proxy reports, we realize that most of them underestimated the shift from textual to multimodal data collection. Our analysis reveals that **video and image scraping now accounts for 42% of total proxy bandwidth consumption**, up from just 18% in 2023. This shift has several implications:

- **Mobile proxies becoming essential** for authentic video content access

- **Bandwidth requirements exploding** – average customer now uses 3.8x more GB than 2023

- **Provider infrastructure strain** – only top-tier providers can handle sustained high-bandwidth loads

- **Pricing pressure** on high-bandwidth plans as margins compress

### [](#The-Hidden-Cost-of-Performance-Gaps)The Hidden Cost of Performance Gaps

A 1.5% difference in success rate may seem negligible but compounds significantly at scale:

**Example scenario: 10M requests/month**

- Provider A (99.8% success): 20,000 failures requiring retries

- Provider B (98.3% success): 170,000 failures requiring retries

- **Additional cost:** 150,000 × retry overhead = $375-$750/month in wasted bandwidth

Similarly, response time differences create real opportunity costs:

- 1 second slower × 10M requests = 2,778 hours = $277,800/year at $100/hour developer time

### [](#Compliance-amp-Ethical-Sourcing)Compliance & Ethical Sourcing

2025 has seen increased scrutiny of proxy sourcing methods. Three mid-market providers were flagged for questionable IP sourcing practices involving:

- Undisclosed VPN user traffic reselling

- Compromised IoT device pools

- Inadequate user consent documentation

Enterprise customers (especially Fortune 500) now require:

- ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II certifications

- GDPR/CCPA compliance with documented consent chains

- Regular third-party audits

- Transparent IP sourcing methodology

Only Bright Data, Oxylabs, and NetNut provide comprehensive compliance documentation packages meeting these requirements.

## FAQ

**What is the average cost of residential proxies in 2025?** Residential proxy prices in 2025 range from $1.50 to $4.00 per GB for most providers, down 70% from 2023 pricing of $8-15/GB. Premium providers like Bright Data charge $2.94-$4.20/GB, while budget options like Decodo and IPRoyal offer $1.50-$2.25/GB at volume. Enterprise customers negotiating annual contracts can achieve rates below $2/GB for commitments exceeding 1TB monthly.  **Which proxy provider has the best performance in 2025?** According to independent Proxyway testing of 1.2 million requests, Oxylabs achieved the highest performance with 99.90% success rate and 0.65-second response time globally. Decodo ranked second at 99.95% success rate with 0.63-second response time. For real-world target success (Amazon, Google, Instagram), Infatica led at 95.2% followed by Decodo at 95.1%. Performance varies by use case, target websites, and geographic region.  **Are datacenter proxies still viable in 2025?** Datacenter proxies remain viable for specific use cases in 2025, achieving 88.5% success rates on real-world targets according to recent testing. They excel for speed-critical applications (0.22-0.29s response times), API scraping, less-protected targets, and cost-sensitive operations at $0.23-$0.60/GB. However, residential proxies are required for protected e-commerce sites, social media platforms, and search engines where datacenter IPs trigger blocks or CAPTCHAs.  **How has AI demand impacted the proxy market?** AI and machine learning applications now represent 25% of total proxy demand in 2025, up from negligible levels in 2023. Every major proxy provider reports AI as a significant or dominant demand driver. AI companies require massive scale (petabytes of data), multimodal content (video, audio, images), real-time freshness for RAG systems, and ethical sourcing with compliance certifications. This has driven 30% YoY increase in AI-focused venture capital funding and prompted providers like Bright Data to launch dedicated AI platforms.  **What are the best proxy providers for enterprise and AI companies?** For enterprise and AI applications, Bright Data and Oxylabs lead with comprehensive features, compliance certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2), and proven infrastructure. Bright Data offers vertical integration with scraper APIs, datasets marketplace, and AI-specific tools like Model Context Protocol servers. Oxylabs consistently ranks highest in performance testing with 99.90% success rates. NetNut excels for large ISP proxy deployments with 1 million IP pool. All three provide transparent ethical sourcing, 24/7 support, and legal defensibility.  **Which proxy providers offer the best value for mid-market businesses?** Decodo (formerly Smartproxy) offers the best value for mid-market businesses, delivering premium-tier performance (99.95% success rate, 0.63s response time) at $1.50-$3.00/GB. SOAX provides unified platform pricing across all proxy types (residential, mobile, ISP, datacenter) starting at $2.00/GB. Massive targets compliance-focused buyers with AppEsteem certification and transparent SDK-based sourcing. All three offer 24/7 support, no minimum commitments on pay-as-you-go plans, and strong performance for $500-$5,000 monthly budgets.  **What is the difference between residential, datacenter, ISP, and mobile proxies?** Residential proxies ($1.50-$4/GB) use real consumer device IPs for highest authenticity and 94-95% success on protected targets. Datacenter proxies ($0.23-$0.60/GB) originate from hosting providers, offering speed and low cost but lower success rates (88.5%) on protected sites. ISP proxies ($1.18-$5/IP/month) combine residential IP ranges with datacenter performance, ideal for video scraping with 50 MB/s throughput. Mobile proxies ($4-$9/GB) use cellular carrier IPs for mobile-specific applications. Choice depends on target websites, required authenticity level, and budget.  **How important is ethical sourcing when choosing a proxy provider?** Ethical sourcing became critical after the May 2024 FBI takedown of 911 S5 botnet (19 million compromised IPs, operator facing 65-year sentence). Legitimate providers now emphasize transparent sourcing through opt-in apps with explicit user consent and compensation. Look for EWDCI certification, ISO 27001, AppEsteem certification, or detailed sourcing documentation. AI companies and enterprises face investor scrutiny and regulatory requirements (GDPR, CCPA) making ethical sourcing non-negotiable. Compliance violations risk $20M+ GDPR fines or 4% of global revenue.  **What proxy pool size do I actually need?** Pool size matters less than IP quality and rotation effectiveness. Providers advertising 100M+ IPs may deliver fewer unique addresses under real usage. Independent testing shows Oxylabs delivered 1.1M unique residential IPs, Decodo 1.15M unique IPs from their advertised pools. For most businesses, 10-50 million quality IPs with good rotation proves sufficient. Focus on success rates (99%+ for residential), response times (<1 second), real-world target performance, and geographic coverage in your target markets rather than raw pool size numbers.  **Should I choose pay-as-you-go or subscription proxy pricing?** Pay-as-you-go suits unpredictable usage, development/testing, seasonal businesses, or operations under 50GB monthly. Non-expiring traffic (IPRoyal, Rayobyte) eliminates waste from unused monthly allocations. Subscriptions offer 15-30% savings for consistent usage exceeding 100GB monthly and provide better support priority. Enterprise contracts (500GB+) achieve deepest discounts but require annual commitments. Calculate total cost including success rates: a 99% success provider at $2/GB costs $2.02 per successful request versus $3.16 for 95% success at $3/GB.

## FAQ

**Why look for Common Crawl alternatives?** Common Crawl provides free web archives but with limitations: 2-3 month data lag, no custom targeting, limited filtering, no real-time data, and complex petabyte-scale processing. Alternatives offer fresh data, custom scraping, and ready-to-use formats.  **Which alternatives provide fresher web data?** Bright Data and Oxylabs offer real-time web data (updated hourly/daily). [Dataset providers](https://scrapingproxies.best/blog/web-data/top-dataset-providers/) like Import.io and ParseHub deliver weekly refreshes. Common Crawl’s 2-3 month lag makes it unsuitable for time-sensitive business intelligence.  **Do Common Crawl alternatives cost money?** Yes—quality web data requires infrastructure. Expect $500-5000/month for custom crawling services, $100-1000/month for dataset subscriptions, or $0.10-5 per page for on-demand scraping. Common Crawl is free but requires significant processing resources.  **Can I get structured data instead of raw HTML?** Yes—most alternatives provide pre-structured data (JSON, CSV, databases) instead of raw WARC files. This eliminates the need for parsing infrastructure and reduces processing time from weeks to hours.  **Which alternative is best for academic research?** For academic budgets: Archive.org’s Wayback Machine (free), Internet Archive datasets, or academic partnerships with Bright Data. For computational research: AWS Public Datasets or Google BigQuery public data (you pay compute only).  **How to migrate from Common Crawl workflows?** Replace WARC processing with API calls, switch from Hadoop/Spark pipelines to provider APIs, use pre-filtered datasets instead of full crawls, and implement incremental updates instead of batch processing. Most providers offer migration support and sample code.  **What’s the minimum scale for Common Crawl alternatives?** Start at 1GB-10GB datasets ($100-500/month) for small projects. Medium scale: 100GB-1TB ($500-2000/month). Enterprise scale: 10TB+ (custom pricing $5000+/month). Common Crawl requires petabyte-scale infrastructure even for small extractions.

## FAQ

**Why look for ScrapeUp alternatives?** ScrapeUp is a newer library with limited documentation, smaller community, and fewer features than mature alternatives. Established libraries offer better error handling, extensive tutorials, larger ecosystems, and proven stability for production environments.  **What’s the most popular alternative to ScrapeUp?** Scrapy is the industry standard (50K+ stars on GitHub, 10+ years mature). [BeautifulSoup](https://scrapingproxies.best/blog/web-scraping/beautifulsoup-web-scraping/) is simplest for beginners. [Selenium](https://scrapingproxies.best/blog/web-scraping/web-scraping-with-selenium/)/[Playwright](https://scrapingproxies.best/blog/web-scraping/web-scraping-with-playwright/) for JavaScript sites. Each has 1000x more Stack Overflow answers and tutorials than ScrapeUp.  **Which alternative is best for beginners?** BeautifulSoup + Requests is the easiest stack: simple API, great documentation, minimal setup. Takes 1-2 hours to learn vs ScrapeUp’s limited resources. For visual approach: try Octoparse or ParseHub instead of coding.  **Do I need to rewrite my ScrapeUp code?** Likely yes. ScrapeUp’s API differs from standard libraries. Migration effort: 2-10 hours depending on project size. Benefit: better long-term maintainability, community support, and job market skills (Scrapy/BeautifulSoup are industry standards).  **Which alternative handles modern websites best?** Playwright or Puppeteer for JavaScript-heavy sites (SPAs, infinite scroll, dynamic content). Selenium is mature but slower. Scrapy-Playwright combines Scrapy’s power with browser automation. ScrapeUp lacks proper JavaScript support.  **What about API rate limiting and retries?** Scrapy has built-in retry middleware, AutoThrottle, and delay management. Scrapy-Playwright adds stealth modes. Requests has retry adapters via urllib3. ScrapeUp lacks sophisticated rate limiting—alternatives prevent bans more effectively.  **Which alternative has best async support?** Scrapy (native async since 2.0), aiohttp for async HTTP, Playwright for async browser automation. These handle 100+ concurrent requests efficiently. ScrapeUp’s async capabilities are limited and poorly documented.

## 4. Selenium

Selenium is a browser automation framework that controls real browsers through code. It was created for web testing but became popular for scraping dynamic sites. Scripts can open pages, click buttons, scroll, fill forms, and wait for elements. This behavior makes Selenium useful when normal HTTP scraping fails to render content. The project supports several languages, including Python, Java, JavaScript, and C sharp. Engineers can run browsers locally or in grid setups across multiple machines. Most testing tools and many cloud providers integrate directly with Selenium. This flexibility means teams can reuse testing knowledge for scraping tasks. The main tradeoff is higher resource cost and more maintenance than simple HTTP based approaches.

### Key Features:

- **Browser Automation:** Control real browsers and simulate clicks, typing, scrolling, and navigation.

- **Multi-Language Support: **Official bindings for Java, Python, JavaScript, C#, Ruby, and more.

- **WebDriver Standard: **Uses the W3C WebDriver spec, so code is portable across browsers.

- **Parallel Execution:** Can be scaled using Selenium Grid or cloud providers to run many browsers at once.

### Pros:

- Excellent for complex, JS-heavy websites.

- Very flexible interaction model (anything a user can do, you can script).

- Huge community, lots of tutorials and tooling.

### Cons:

- Heavy on CPU and RAM; not ideal for millions of pages.

- Easier to detect than pure HTTP requests unless hardened.

- Requires WebDriver setup, version matching, and ongoing maintenance.

### Pricing:

- Selenium itself is **open source and free**.

- You still pay for servers, proxies, and any anti-detection / CAPTCHA services.

## 5. BeautifulSoup

[BeautifulSoup](https://scrapingproxies.best/blog/web-scraping/beautifulsoup-web-scraping/) is a [Python](https://scrapingproxies.best/blog/web-scraping/web-scraping-python/) library that helps you read and process HTML or XML files. It converts raw markup into a structured format that’s easy to explore. You can search for tags, pull out text, or clean up messy web pages quickly. Most developers use it with the Requests library to download and parse pages in one workflow. Its main advantage is simplicity and flexibility. Even beginners can start scraping data after a short time. It also handles broken or incomplete HTML gracefully. However, BeautifulSoup doesn’t handle network requests, concurrency, or scheduling. You must manage those parts yourself. As it focuses only on parsing, it stays lightweight and reliable, making it a popular choice for web data extraction in Python.

### Key Features:

- **HTML/XML Parsing:** Provides a parse tree for HTML and XML documents.

- **DOM Navigation:** Lets you search, filter, and navigate tags using simple methods.

- **Tolerant Parser:** Handles broken HTML (“tag soup”) gracefully.

- **Parser Flexibility: **Works with html.parser, lxml, or other underlying parsers.

### Pros:

- Very easy for beginners.

- Great for small to medium scraping projects.

- Combines well with requests and other HTTP libraries.

### Cons:

- No built-in crawler, concurrency, or scheduling.

- Not optimized alone for very large-scale scraping.

- Python-only.

### Pricing:

- BeautifulSoup is **open source and free** (available via beautifulsoup4 on PyPI).

## 6. Axios 

Axios is a popular HTTP client for JavaScript and Node.js. It uses promises and async functions to keep code readable and modern. Developers call APIs, fetch pages, and send JSON payloads through a simple interface. The same code can often run in the browser and on the server. Interceptors allow global handling of headers, authentication, and logging. Many scraping setups in Node.js use Axios to download pages before handing them to a parser. It focuses on network concerns and allows you to pick other tools for parsing and browser automation. This design keeps Axios lightweight, flexible, and easy to fit into existing JavaScript projects.

### Key Features:

- **Promise-Based HTTP: **Makes GET, POST, and other requests with async/await or Promises.

- **Isomorphic Usage:** Same code can run in Node.js and in the browser.

- **Interceptors:** Allows you to intercept and modify requests or responses globally.

- **Data Transformation: **Automatically serializes and transforms request and response data.

### Pros:

- Simple, readable API for JavaScript developers.

- Works well with Cheerio, Puppeteer, and other scraping tools.

- Easy to add custom headers, cookies, and timeouts.

### Cons:

- Provides only HTTP; no parsing, crawling, or anti-bot logic.

- JavaScript-only; not useful outside that ecosystem.

- You must handle retries, proxy rotation, and blocking yourself.

### Pricing:

- Axios is **open source and free** under the MIT license.

## 7. Python Requests

Requests is a popular Python library for sending HTTP requests easily. It turns complex networking tasks into simple, readable code. Developers use it to send GET or POST requests, add headers, include query parameters, and manage cookies. It’s also great for maintaining sessions across multiple requests using session objects. Many web scraping projects rely on Requests to fetch web pages, then pass them to BeautifulSoup or lxml for parsing. The library focuses on simplicity and stability, not advanced features like crawling, concurrency, or JavaScript execution. You handle those parts with other tools or custom scripts. This clean, minimal design makes Requests ideal for developers who want full control over their scraping logic without dealing with unnecessary complexity.

### Key Features:

- **Simple HTTP API: **Easy functions for GET, POST, and other verbs with minimal boilerplate.

- **Session Handling: **Built-in session objects with cookie persistence.

- **SSL Verification:** Browser-style SSL checks, redirects, and connection pooling.

- **Proxy Support:** Easy configuration for HTTP, HTTPS, and SOCKS proxies.

### Pros:

- Very easy to read and maintain.

- Works perfectly with BeautifulSoup, lxml, or custom parsers.

- Huge adoption, lots of community content and examples.

### Cons:

- Synchronous; you must add extra tools for concurrency.

- No built-in crawling, throttling, or scheduling.

- No automatic JS rendering or anti-bot support.

### Pricing:

- requests is **open source and free**, licensed under Apache 2.0.

## 8. Cheerio

Cheerio is a server side HTML parsing library for Node.js. It offers a jQuery like API without running a real browser. Developers load an HTML string and then query it using familiar CSS selectors. This makes extraction of titles, links, prices, and other elements straightforward. Many scraping stacks pair Cheerio with Axios or another HTTP client. The combination replaces jQuery usage in the browser with a light and fast parser in Node.js. Cheerio focuses only on DOM manipulation and does not fetch pages or execute JavaScript. This narrow focus keeps it efficient and predictable. Teams that already know jQuery usually adapt to Cheerio quickly and can build reliable parsers using existing selector knowledge.

### Key Features:

- **jQuery-Like Selectors: **Uses CSS/jQuery-style selectors to find and manipulate elements.

- **Fast DOM Model: **Uses a simple, consistent DOM for efficient parsing and manipulation.

- **HTML/XML Support: **Parses most HTML and XML markup in Node.js environments.

- **Server-Side Focus:** Designed for Node.js and server-side scraping workflows.

### Pros:

- Very familiar to anyone who has used jQuery.

- Lightweight and fast compared to running a browser.

- Great for converting raw HTML from Axios or other clients into structured data.

### Cons:

- No HTTP client; you must bring your own (Axios, node-fetch, etc.).

- Does not execute JavaScript.

- Only useful in JavaScript / Node.js projects.

### Pricing:

- Cheerio is **open source and free** (MIT license).

## Conclusion

Scrapy is useful, but it cannot handle every challenge on today’s web. Modern sites use strong anti-bot tools, dynamic content, and constant changes that push Scrapy to its limits. The tools in this list solve different parts of that problem. Bright Data and ZenRows help you avoid blocks. Apify manages scheduling and automation. Selenium handles complex pages that need real browser actions. BeautifulSoup, Requests, Axios, and Cheerio give you simple building blocks when you want complete control. Pick the tools that fit your goals, your skills, and the sites you target. Stop relying on one framework for every job and build a smarter stack.

## FAQ

**Why consider Scrapy alternatives?** Scrapy has steep learning curve (2-4 weeks), complex architecture (spiders, pipelines, middlewares), and poor JavaScript support without plugins. Alternatives offer simpler APIs for small projects, native JavaScript handling, or managed infrastructure for non-developers.  **What’s the easiest alternative to Scrapy?** BeautifulSoup + Requests is simplest: 3 lines of code vs Scrapy’s 50+ line spider. Learn in 2 hours vs 2 weeks. Perfect for one-off scraping tasks. For visual approach: Octoparse or ParseHub require zero coding.  **Which alternatives handle JavaScript better?** Playwright and Puppeteer have native browser automation (Scrapy requires scrapy-playwright plugin). Selenium is mature but slower. Bright Data and Apify provide managed JavaScript rendering. All avoid Scrapy’s middleware complexity.  **Do I need Scrapy’s power for small projects?** No—Requests + BeautifulSoup handles 80% of use cases with 10x simpler code. Use Scrapy only for: large-scale crawling (1000+ pages/hour), complex pipelines, distributed scraping, or sophisticated middleware needs.  **Which alternative scales best?** For cloud scaling: Apify (serverless, auto-scale) or Bright Data (managed infrastructure). For distributed crawling: [Crawlee](https://scrapingproxies.best/blog/web-scraping/crawlee-web-scraping/) (TypeScript) or custom Kubernetes deployments. Scrapy-Redis scales horizontally but requires DevOps expertise.  **What about commercial Scrapy alternatives?** Bright Data Web Scraper IDE (visual + code), Apify (managed Scrapy-like platform), ScrapingBee (API-based, no infrastructure), Zyte (Scrapy creators’ commercial platform). All offer easier setup than self-hosted Scrapy.  **Which alternative has better documentation?** Requests and BeautifulSoup have excellent docs + 10,000+ tutorials. Playwright has comprehensive guides + examples. Bright Data offers live chat support. Scrapy’s docs are technical and assume advanced Python knowledge.

## FAQ

**What are Edge proxies and how do they work with Microsoft Edge?** Edge proxies are intermediary servers specifically configured to work seamlessly with Microsoft Edge browser, routing your internet traffic through different IP addresses while maintaining Edge’s built-in security features and performance optimizations. They work by intercepting Edge’s network requests at the system or browser level, redirecting connections through proxy servers before reaching destination websites. Edge proxies are unique because they must be compatible with Chromium’s network stack (Edge’s underlying engine) while respecting Windows security policies and Edge’s modern features like SmartScreen, tracking prevention, and Collections. Unlike VPNs that tunnel all system traffic, Edge proxies give granular control—you can proxy only Edge while leaving other applications with direct connections. This is crucial for professionals who need proxied browsing for work (market research, competitive analysis, content testing) while maintaining normal connections for other tools. Premium Edge proxies from providers like Bright Data automatically configure Edge’s proxy settings through APIs or browser extensions, eliminating complex manual configuration and ensuring compatibility with Edge’s frequent updates and security patches.  **Can I use proxies with Microsoft Edge’s built-in security features?** Yes, [premium proxies](https://scrapingproxies.best/premium-proxies/) enhance rather than compromise Microsoft Edge’s built-in security features when properly configured. Edge’s SmartScreen protection, tracking prevention, and password monitor continue functioning normally with proxies because these operate at different network layers—SmartScreen analyzes site reputation, tracking prevention blocks cookies, while proxies simply change your routing path. The key is choosing proxy providers that support HTTPS connections with proper SSL/TLS certificates, ensuring encryption remains intact between Edge and destination sites. Bright Data, IPRoyal, and Oxylabs all maintain full compatibility with Edge’s security stack, providing certificate validation and encrypted connections that preserve SmartScreen functionality. However, avoid free or low-quality proxies that strip HTTPS headers or inject certificates—these break Edge’s security entirely. Professional configuration: Use [SOCKS5 proxies](https://scrapingproxies.best/socks5-proxies/) with authentication for maximum security, enable Edge’s Do Not Track” even with proxies (some sites honor this) and combine proxies with Edge’s password manager and Defender SmartScreen for defense-in-depth. Premium residential proxies actually improve security by masking your real IP from trackers while Edge’s security features protect against malicious sites—giving you both privacy and protection simultaneously.”  **Do Edge proxies work with Windows authentication and enterprise features?** Yes, enterprise-grade Edge proxies fully support Windows authentication and Microsoft 365 integration, making them suitable for business environments using Active Directory, Azure AD, and Intune management. Premium providers like Bright Data and Oxylabs offer NTLM and Kerberos authentication passthrough, allowing Edge to authenticate to proxy servers using Windows credentials without separate login prompts. This is critical for enterprises where IT manages proxy configurations centrally through Group Policy or Intune, pushing settings to all Edge browsers without user intervention. Edge proxies integrate seamlessly with Windows SSO (Single Sign-On), maintaining your authenticated Microsoft 365 sessions while routing traffic through proxies—essential for remote workers accessing SharePoint, Teams, and Outlook through Edge while connected via corporate proxies. For hybrid work environments, proxy providers offer PAC (Proxy Auto-Configuration) files that automatically select proxy servers based on destination URLs, allowing direct connections to internal resources while proxying external sites. Most enterprise Edge proxy configurations use Windows Registry modifications or GPO settings to configure system-wide proxy settings that Edge inherits automatically, ensuring consistent behavior across all managed devices while maintaining security compliance and audit trails required by IT departments.  **Which proxy type works best for browsing with Microsoft Edge?** Residential proxies work best for browsing with Microsoft Edge because they provide real user IP addresses that websites trust completely, ensuring you experience the web as a normal visitor without CAPTCHAs, access blocks, or degraded content. Premium residential providers like Bright Data (150M+ IPs) and IPRoyal (32M+ IPs) offer seamless integration with Edge’s Chromium engine, delivering 99%+ success rates even on security-conscious sites that aggressively block datacenter IPs. For general browsing and streaming, sticky residential proxies maintain consistent IP addresses for session duration (10-30 minutes), preventing the annoying logouts and verification prompts that occur with aggressive IP rotation. For data collection and automated tasks in Edge (price monitoring, competitive research), rotating residential proxies automatically change IPs between requests, preventing detection and rate limiting. ISP proxies offer an excellent middle ground—residential legitimacy with datacenter speeds—ideal for professional browsing where performance matters (trading platforms, web development, QA testing). Datacenter proxies work for basic Edge browsing but trigger more CAPTCHAs and blocks. Mobile proxies provide maximum anonymity but are overkill for standard browsing. Most users should start with sticky residential proxies for the best balance of performance, reliability, and natural browsing experience.  **How much do Edge-compatible proxies cost?** Edge-compatible proxy pricing in 2025 ranges from $2 to $8 per GB depending on proxy type and provider capabilities. Budget-friendly options include IPRoyal’s ISP proxies at $2 per proxy with unlimited bandwidth—excellent for personal browsing and small-scale use without monthly data caps. Mid-tier providers like ProxyRack offer rotating residential proxies from $1.50 per GB, suitable for moderate usage including streaming, social media management, and content testing in Edge. Premium providers like Bright Data and Oxylabs charge $3.50-8 per GB but deliver 99.95%+ success rates, 195-country coverage, and enterprise-grade reliability essential for business-critical browsing. For typical personal use (browsing, streaming, social media), budget 5-10GB monthly at $15-30. Small businesses conducting market research or content testing should plan for 25-50GB at $50-120 monthly. Enterprise users running automated browser workflows in Edge need 100GB+ with custom pricing starting around $350-600 monthly. Most providers offer pay-as-you-go options perfect for testing Edge compatibility before committing to monthly plans. Consider your needs: casual browsing requires 5-10GB; professional use demands 25-50GB; enterprise automation needs 100GB+ with dedicated support. Free trials (3-7 days) let you validate Edge compatibility with your specific use cases.  **Can I configure Edge proxies for specific websites or domains?** Yes, Microsoft Edge supports sophisticated proxy configurations that route specific websites through proxies while allowing direct connections for others—this is called PAC (Proxy Auto-Configuration) or split-tunneling. Premium proxy providers like Bright Data offer pre-built PAC files that you can import into Edge’s settings, automatically proxying target sites (e.g., competitors, research targets, geo-restricted content) while keeping other traffic direct for optimal performance. Manual configuration in Edge: Navigate to Settings → System → Open your computer’s proxy settings → Configure automatic proxy setup with PAC file URL or manual proxy settings with bypass list. Professional approach: Use extension-based proxy managers like ProxySwitcher or FoxyProxy that integrate with Edge, allowing you to define rules like “proxy all *.amazon.* domains through Residential IPs” while browsing internal company sites directly. This is essential for researchers who need proxied access to competitive sites while maintaining normal speeds for productivity tools. Advanced users can write custom PAC files with JavaScript logic: if destination matches pattern, use proxy; else, use direct connection. For businesses, centralized PAC files hosted on internal servers allow IT to manage proxy rules across all Edge installations without touching individual computers. This domain-specific routing dramatically reduces proxy costs by proxying only necessary traffic while maintaining full-speed access to frequently-used sites.  **Which Edge proxy provider offers the best browser integration?** Bright Data provides the best Edge integration with its proprietary Proxy Manager extension that seamlessly configures proxy settings, manages authentication, and monitors connection quality directly within Edge’s interface. The extension offers one-click switching between datacenter, residential, ISP, and mobile proxies without manual reconfiguration, perfect for professionals needing different proxy types for different tasks. Bright Data’s Edge extension also provides real-time success rate monitoring, automatic failover when proxies fail, and geo-targeting controls—letting you select specific countries or cities without leaving your browser. For users preferring system-level configuration, IPRoyal offers comprehensive Windows integration guides specifically for Edge, including PowerShell scripts that configure proxies through Windows settings that Edge automatically inherits. Smartproxy (now Decodo) provides a dedicated browser extension supporting Edge with features like automatic cookie management and session persistence, crucial for maintaining logged-in states across proxy switches. For enterprise environments, Oxylabs offers API-based configuration that pushes proxy settings to Edge via Windows Registry modifications, ideal for IT departments managing hundreds of Edge installations. Choose based on use case: individual users should use Bright Data’s extension for convenience; IT administrators should implement IPRoyal or Oxylabs system-level configurations; power users wanting granular control should use FoxyProxy extension with any provider.

GitHub proxies are essential for developers, researchers, and businesses that need reliable, uninterrupted access to GitHub’s vast code repository ecosystem while maintaining security and avoiding detection.  **Which types of proxies work best for GitHub scraping?** Residential proxies work best for GitHub scraping because they use real user IP addresses that GitHub’s systems trust, making them virtually undetectable even during intensive data collection. They’re ideal for continuous monitoring tasks and automated workflows. Datacenter proxies can work for basic GitHub access but carry higher detection risks during scraping operations. For most use cases, rotating residential proxies are recommended because they automatically switch IPs between requests, preventing pattern detection. Second, free proxies are typically blacklisted by GitHub’s security systems, resulting in immediate IP bans that can affect your entire organization’s access. Third, they have abysmal success rates (below 10%) because hundreds of users share the same IPs, making them worthless for actual work. Fourth, free proxies lack encryption, exposing your source code and sensitive data to man-in-the-middle attacks. Premium GitHub proxies from trusted providers cost as little as $15-50/month for personal projects, a minimal investment that protects your code, credentials, and productivity. The security and reliability of paid proxies justify the cost exponentially compared to the catastrophic risks of free alternatives.  **Do GitHub proxies work with Git commands and CI/CD?** Yes, GitHub proxies work seamlessly with Git commands and CI/CD pipelines when properly configured. First, use rotating residential proxies from providers like Bright Data with 150M+ IPs, ensuring each request comes from a different address. Second, implement realistic delays between requests (3-5 seconds minimum) to mimic human browsing patterns rather than aggressive bot behavior. Third, respect GitHub’s rate limits (5,000 requests/hour for authenticated users, 60/hour for unauthenticated) by monitoring your usage through headers. Fourth, use proper User-Agent strings that match real browsers and rotate them periodically. Fifth, authenticate your requests with GitHub tokens when possible, as authenticated requests receive higher rate limits and appear more legitimate. ## FAQ

**Why do Airbnb scraping tasks need proxies?** Airbnb has aggressive anti-bot protection that blocks datacenter IPs and rate limits suspicious activity. Residential proxies with proper rotation bypass these controls and maintain session continuity.  **Which proxy type is best for Airbnb?** Residential proxies with sticky sessions (10-30 minutes) for listing scraping. ISP proxies work for search/browse. Avoid datacenter IPs—they have 90%+ block rates on Airbnb.  **Do I need geo-targeting for Airbnb?** Yes, critical. Airbnb shows different prices, availability, and listings based on visitor location. Target the specific city/country you’re monitoring for accurate pricing data and local inventory.  **What’s a safe scraping rate for Airbnb?** Start at 1-2 requests per second per IP with 3-5 second delays between listing views. Airbnb monitors velocity and pattern. Scale gradually while monitoring for CAPTCHA or blocks.  **Can I manage multiple Airbnb host accounts with proxies?** Yes—use dedicated residential IPs per account with unique device fingerprints and cookies. Never log into multiple accounts from same IP. Airbnb’s fraud detection links accounts via IP patterns.  **How to handle Airbnb CAPTCHAs?** Use high-quality residential IPs from major ISPs, maintain consistent sessions, add random delays, and integrate CAPTCHA solving services (2Captcha, AntiCaptcha) for automated workflows.  **Best concurrency for Airbnb scraping?** 3-5 concurrent threads per residential IP maximum. Higher concurrency triggers velocity limits. Use IP pools of 20-50 IPs for large-scale scraping with proper rotation logic.

## FAQ

**Why choose Orange proxies specifically?** Orange is France’s largest mobile operator with 28M+ subscribers and strong presence in Europe/Africa. Orange IPs provide authentic French mobile fingerprints and bypass [French geo-restrictions](https://scrapingproxies.best/ip-locations/france/) effectively.  **Which regions does Orange cover?** Primary: France (all departments), Spain, Poland, Belgium. Secondary: Romania, Slovakia, Morocco, Senegal, Ivory Coast. Orange proxies give access to French and Francophone content with carrier-grade trust.  **Mobile vs ISP proxies from Orange?** Mobile proxies use Orange’s 4G/5G network (higher trust, premium pricing $8-12/GB). ISP proxies use Orange’s fiber/DSL network (good for web scraping, cheaper at $3-6/GB). Choose based on target detection sophistication.  **What session duration for Orange mobile IPs?** 10-20 minutes optimal. French platforms expect longer mobile sessions than US markets. Too-short rotation (< 5 min) triggers fraud detection; too-long (> 30 min) wastes premium carrier bandwidth.  **Can I target specific French cities?** Yes—major providers offer city-level targeting: Paris, Marseille, Lyon, Toulouse, Nice, Nantes. City targeting helps with local content, pricing variations, and regional inventory on French e-commerce sites.  **Do Orange proxies work outside France?** Orange IPs work globally for accessing French content. However, French sites may show different content to Orange IPs accessing from abroad. Best results when Orange IP geo-location matches target site’s expected user location.  **Cost comparison: Orange vs other French carriers?** Orange: $8-12/GB (premium). SFR: $7-10/GB. Bouygues: $6-9/GB. Free Mobile: $5-8/GB. Orange commands premium pricing due to market dominance and higher trust scores on French platforms.

Premium providers offer Verizon Business IPs. Avoid providers using Verizon MVNOs (Visible, Tracfone)—these have lower trust scores.  **Can I get 5G Verizon proxies?** Yes—premium providers offer Verizon 5G UWB (Ultra Wideband) IPs in major metros. 5G IPs cost 20-30% more ($10-15/GB vs $7-10/GB for 4G) but deliver faster speeds and newest device fingerprints.  **What US states have best Verizon coverage?** Verizon covers all 50 states. Best for: Northeast (NY, NJ, PA, MA), Mid-Atlantic (VA, MD), Midwest (IL, OH, MI), California, Florida, Texas. City-level targeting available for 200+ metros.  **Verizon vs AT&T vs T-Mobile proxies?** Verizon: Highest trust, most coverage, premium pricing ($8-12/GB).
