## FAQ

**What are telecom proxies?** Telecom proxies are IPs sourced directly from mobile network operators (AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, Orange, Vodafone). They provide authentic carrier-grade mobile IPs that websites trust more than [residential or datacenter](https://scrapingproxies.best/blog/proxy-101/datacenter-vs-residential-proxies/) IPs.  **Why use telecom proxies vs residential?** Telecom proxies offer carrier-specific targeting, higher trust scores on mobile-optimized sites, authentic mobile fingerprints, and compliance with carrier-based geo-restrictions. Success rates are 15-30% higher than residential.  **Which carriers are available through proxy providers?** Major US carriers (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, Sprint), European carriers (Orange, Vodafone, O2, Deutsche Telekom), Asian carriers (China Mobile, NTT DoCoMo, SK Telecom), and regional carriers in 50+ countries.  **What use cases need telecom proxies?** Mobile app testing across carriers, carrier-specific content scraping, mobile ad verification, SMS verification services, mobile game testing, carrier billing systems, and mobile-first platform scraping.  **Rotating vs sticky sessions for telecom proxies?** Sticky sessions (5-20 minutes) for app testing and authenticated flows. Rotating for public mobile web scraping. Telecom IPs are premium—optimize session length to balance cost and effectiveness.  **How much do telecom carrier proxies cost?** Premium pricing: $5-15/GB for major carrier IPs. US carriers (Verizon, AT&T) cost more ($8-15/GB). Asian/European carriers range $5-10/GB. Budget $200-500/month for moderate usage.  **Are telecom proxies legal and compliant?** Yes, when sourced ethically. Providers should obtain IPs through legitimate carrier partnerships or licensed mobile device pools. Avoid providers using SIM farms or unauthorized carrier access.

## FAQ

**Why do I need Indosat proxies specifically?** Indosat is one of Indonesia’s major mobile carriers with 60M+ subscribers. Indosat proxies provide authentic Indonesian mobile IPs that bypass geo-restrictions and avoid detection on Indonesian platforms.  **Which proxy type works best for Indosat?** Mobile proxies with real Indosat carrier IPs deliver highest success rates. Residential IPs can work for light browsing, but carrier-specific IPs provide better trust scores on Indonesian sites.  **Do I need city-level targeting in Indonesia?** Yes—Indonesia’s archipelago means significant regional differences. City-level targeting (Jakarta, Surabaya, Bandung) improves local content accuracy and reduces fraud detection.  **What session lengths work for Indosat mobile proxies?** 5-15 minutes for most use cases. Indonesian platforms expect mobile session patterns similar to real users. Too-short rotation triggers suspicion; too-long sessions waste premium mobile bandwidth.  **Can datacenter proxies work for Indonesia?** Rarely. Indonesian platforms are aggressive about detecting non-mobile traffic. Datacenter IPs have 80%+ failure rates. Always prefer mobile or high-quality residential IPs with Indonesian carrier ASNs.  **How to avoid bans with Indosat proxies?** Use realistic mobile user agents (Android 10+), respect rate limits (2-3 req/sec per IP), rotate between multiple Indosat IPs, and mimic natural mobile browsing patterns with delays.  **What’s the cost of Indosat mobile proxies?** Expect $3-8/GB for quality Indosat carrier IPs. Cheaper options often use VPN-based solutions that get blocked quickly. Budget $100-300/month for moderate scraping needs.

## FAQ

**Why do AliExpress tasks need proxies?** To bypass geo-blocks, avoid rate limits on product data, and maintain persistent sessions for price tracking.  **Residential vs datacenter for AliExpress?** Residential IPs have higher success on protected endpoints; datacenter works for public product pages.  **Should I target China geos specifically?** Yes—China IPs see better pricing, fuller catalogs, and fewer anti-bot triggers.  **What session length for cart/checkout?** 10–20 minute sticky sessions prevent mid-purchase IP changes that break state.  **Can I rotate on every request?** For catalog scraping—yes. For login or dropship automation—use sticky sessions.  **How to handle CAPTCHA?** Use high-quality residential/mobile IPs, add delays between requests, and integrate CAPTCHA solvers if needed.  **Best concurrency for AliExpress?** Start with 2–5 req/s per IP and scale based on success rates; AliExpress is moderately aggressive.

## FAQ

**Why consider Proxy-Seller alternatives?** If you need larger IP pools, better geo-coverage, advanced rotation, or more competitive pricing structures.  **Which alternatives scale best?** Bright Data and Oxylabs for enterprise; Smartproxy/IPRoyal for SMBs; Webshare for budget.  **Are datacenter alternatives cheaper?** Yes—datacenter pools cost 10–20x less than residential but have lower success on protected targets.  **Datacenter vs residential for alternatives?** Datacenter is cheap for basic tasks; residential/ISP yield higher success on protected targets.  **Can I mix providers?** Yes—multi-vendor routing adds resilience and cost control.  **What migration pitfalls to avoid?** Match protocols, rotate DNS/auth creds safely, and A/B test success rate before full cutover.  **How to compare true cost?** Normalize to $/successful request or $/GB including error-retries.
